title: Uttam Nagar Food Tour | Delhi Street Food | Veggie Paaji
description:
Join Veggie Paaji on an exciting food adventure in Uttam Nagar, West Delhi! In this latest episode of our Delhi Food Series, we're diving deep into the vibrant street food scene to uncover "Uttam Nagar Special" dishes, from unique momos to authentic dhaba-style meals.

Highlights of our culinary journey:

King's Momos: Indulge in crispy Kurkure Momos [01:59], flavorful Afghani Momos [02:40], spicy Tandoori Momos [02:40], and tender Tandoori Chaap [02:50]. Don't miss their delicious Dahi Bhalla [00:56]!

Location: King's Momos, Uttam Nagar

Bhagwandas Chole Tikki: Savor the classic combination of crispy Chole Tikki [09:41] with a spicy chickpea curry.

Location: Bhagwandas Chole Tikki, Uttam Nagar (This is a street vendor, so the precise location may vary, but it's on Arya Samaj Road).

Anand Vaishno Dhaba: Experience authentic North Indian cuisine with their rich Special Chana Masala [15:22], creamy Dal Makhni [15:24], and soft Butter Naan [15:25].

Location: Anand Vaishno Dhaba, Uttam Nagar

Scoops Ice Cream, Shakes & Mocktails: End your food tour with a refreshing Oreo Cone Softie [19:46] or a classic Vanilla Softie [19:59] at this 24/7 spot!

Location: Scoops, Uttam Nagar

Come along as we explore the best of Uttam Nagar's street food, offering genuine reviews and a taste of Delhi's incredible culinary diversity!

description:
Golden Fish Kitchen

In today’s video, we take you to the heart of Dombivli, where we discovered an absolute hidden gem — Golden Fish Kitchen, a humble street-side eatery run by a beautiful and hardworking couple. They serve authentic Agri-style seafood and non-veg delicacies that are bursting with coastal flavors and tradition.

We had the chance to try some of their best-selling dishes, including the Surmai Fish Fry, Pomfret Fry, Bombil Fry, and the rich, flavorful Prawns Curry. Each bite was a perfect blend of spice, crunch, and freshness. We also indulged in the unique Jawla Wadi and the spicy, lip-smacking Jawla Chutney, both of which added a rustic charm to the meal.

What truly sets this place apart is not just the food, but the love and dedication the couple pours into every dish. Their warmth and hospitality make the entire experience even more memorable.

If you’re a seafood or non-veg lover and want to explore the true taste of Agri cuisine, Golden Fish Kitchen is a must-visit. Don’t miss out on this flavorful journey through Dombivli’s street food scene!

title: Best Lucknow Brunch Food Tour : Sursuri / Bandook Chaat, Bun Chola, Bakse Wale Khaste, Malai Makhan
description:
Lucknow is often celebrated for its rich Awadhi cuisine, but the city also boasts a thriving vegetarian street food culture that deserves equal recognition. On this special food tour, we teamed up with Priyank, a passionate local food explorer, to experience a classic Lucknawi vegetarian brunch. Priyank, known for his insightful vlogs, guided us through some of the city's most beloved breakfast spots, offering a glimpse into its vibrant morning food scene.  

Our first stop was a small but iconic tea stall, M/S Ram Kewal Tea Stall, located on Maqbara Road in Hazratganj. A favorite among locals, this place serves a comforting cup of tea made by mixing tea liquor with milk. The tea was paired with bun makhan, generously slathered with unsalted white butter sourced from a local dairy. We also tried their samosa and sihal, a lesser-known but delicious deep-fried snack that complemented the tea perfectly.  

Next, we made our way to Gupta Ji Khaste Wale at Chowk Kotwali, Gol Darwaza, Chowk, where we tried a special breakfast dish called bakse wale khasta. These khasta kachoris are stored and served from metallic trunks, giving them their distinctive name. Accompanied by dry masala wale aalu, this dish is immensely popular, and the stock often runs out between 7 and 10 in the morning.  

At Gol Darwaza, Chowk, we visited Malai Makhan Corner to sample the quintessential winter delicacy, malai makhan. This creamy, airy sweet, infused with a subtle hint of cardamom, was a delightful experience. Many vendors sell it in this area, but the one we visited had recently hosted actor Diljit Dosanjh, further cementing its reputation.  

Moving ahead, we stopped at Sewak Ram Misthan Bhandar near Kalli Ji Ram Mandir in Sarrafa Bazaar, Chowk. This old sweet and snack shop is known for its traditional preparations made entirely in ghee. Here, we tried the poori and sabzi combo, a dish that evoked the flavors of food found in the holy cities of Uttar Pradesh. We also tasted jalebi dahi and two seasonal varieties of ladoo, each showcasing the richness of Lucknawi sweets.  

While heading to our next stop, we came across an intriguing roadside stall named Badnaam Chole Stall at Gwynne Road in Aminabad Market. True to its name, the stall had an element of curiosity around it. We tried their chole suhal and bun chole makhan, both offering a unique take on the classic chole preparation.  

Our final destination was Pandit Chaat Corner near Khun Khun Ji Jewellers in Aminabad. A hidden gem in the city’s bustling chaat scene, this place is known for its batashe, sursuri chaat, matar chaat, and a few other specialties. The owner, Kalyan ji, welcomed us warmly and treated us to a variety of dishes, each bursting with distinct flavors and textures. His hospitality and passion for food made the experience even more memorable.  

This food tour through Lucknow’s vegetarian delights offered a refreshing perspective on the city’s diverse culinary heritage. Each stop added a unique layer to our understanding of its street food culture, making it an experience worth savoring.

title: MORADABAD Non Veg Food Tour I Biscuit Wali Gali + Shabnam Double Roti + Keeme ki Poori + HabshiHalwa
description:
Join us on an unforgettable Iftar Food Walk in Moradabad, where centuries-old culinary traditions blend seamlessly with the warmth of its people. Guided by our gracious host Sayeed Ahmed, we spent an evening exploring lanes filled with aromas, stories, and a deep sense of community during Ramzan.

Our journey began in the iconic Biscuit Wali Gali in Kath Ki Puliya, home to Shabnam Walon Ki Mehak Bread. This narrow bylane, famous for its baked goods, introduced us to the unique breads that become an essential part of iftar in Moradabad. From airy loaves to dense, flavour-packed varieties, each bread reflects a local tradition and a purpose on the Ramzan table.

We then headed to Baburam Misthan Bhandar in Bartan Bazaar, a legendary establishment that has been serving the city since 1891. Stepping inside felt like stepping back in time. Here we tasted their classic jalebi, rabri and khurchan, all prepared in pure desi ghee. Every bite reminded us why this shop still stands tall after more than a century, consistency, craft, and love.

The highlight of our walk was an intimate iftar at the home of Dr. Rafey Fahim and Dr. Anas Fahim. As conversations flowed, we learned about Moradabad’s traditions around sheri (pre-dawn meal). Their table was a reflection of the family’s love for food, aloo ki pakodi, samose, jalebi, chicken fry, fruit chaat, chole, keeme ki puri, biryani, zarda, bihari dishes, dahi phulki, and a fragrant homemade biryani. A feast rooted in personal preferences, nostalgic cravings, and Ramzan warmth. Being welcomed into their home was truly special.

Post a small breather, we resumed our food trail at Zaitoon, Lajpat Nagar, known for blending Middle Eastern flavours with local tastes. We savoured gola kebab, chicken tikka seasoned with sumac-thyme-basil, al fahm, and their popular parda biryani. The sight of freshly grilled kebabs and trays of festive sweets added yet another layer to our Ramzan experience.

A short stroll brought us to Haji Abdul Jabbar Dairy at Indra Chowk, a beloved Sheri Milk Point. Generations have stopped here for nourishing milk-based drinks that keep them energised through the fast. It’s places like this that hold the emotional weight of Ramzan memories.

From there, our walk continued to Salman Food Chicken Corner for their shawarma and khaboos, followed by Gulshan-e-Karim, a legendary Mughlai shop established in 1901. Here we watched fresh seekh kebabs come straight off the skewers, accompanied by timeless dishes that define Moradabad’s Mughlai identity.

At Rampur Sweets Corner, an 80-year-old establishment on Nai Sarak, we explored sweets that trace their origins to Rampur, katli, habsi halwa, angoor dana, and the unique aohan halwa. These sweets, prepared year-round, carry flavours not commonly found outside this region.

Kacheri Road welcomed us with two major stops. First, Mezban Shama Chicken Corner (est. 2007), where we tried their much-loved non-vegetarian delicacies, chicken seekh kebab, roomali roti, chicken korma, and tawa chicken. Each dish was bold, hearty, and unapologetically flavourful.

Then, The Pahelwan Food, where Zaheer took us through their menu and family legacy. His father, a pehelwan, crafted many of the recipes still used today. Since 1983, this shop has been known for its rich use of ghee and their signature roasted chicken, a dish that carries generations of expertise.

We ended the night with a comforting cup of tea, the perfect wrap to a long, flavour-packed walk through Moradabad’s lanes.

This episode isn’t just about food, it’s about people opening their hearts, preserving traditions, and sharing their Ramzan with us. Step into the spirit of Moradabad and experience its iftar culture, one delicious stop at a time.

title: Kasol to Manali Via Naggar Food Trip | Naggar Castle Bakery Rum ball + Cheese Spinach/Kothey Momo
description:
After spending a peaceful day in Kasol, we set off for Manali the next morning with our gracious host Khushboo, for whom Himachal truly feels like a second home. We began our day with breakfast at Kailasha - The Himalayan Village. It was raining gently, and the meal felt soulful and comforting. The spread included assorted fruits, garlic bread, dalia pulao, idli, and coffee - all homestyle and served in a serene setting.
On our way to Manali, we made a quick stop at Naggar Castle, a popular and historic site known for its beautiful wood and stone architecture and panoramic views of the valley. Just nearby, we stumbled upon a charming homemade bakery that’s a hit with tourists. Their rum ball and carrot cake are quick to sell out – and we were lucky to get our hands on them.
Not long after, we noticed a makeshift honey stall along the road. The owner explained how honey is cultivated using artificial hives inside boxes, which are later processed and reused. We tasted three types of honey, each one unique in flavor.
We then reached Sunbloom Cafe and met its passionate owner who shared the journey of how this scenic cafe came into being. The outdoor seating was inviting and peaceful. We enjoyed fresh juice and delicious spinach momos before continuing on.
By the time we arrived in Manali, it was evening and we were hungry. We kept dinner simple - comforting dal roti at Beas Punjabi Dhaba. A satisfying end to a day full of scenic views, and soulful food.

title: Ep 11, Best ITO Street Food Walk I Sardarji Paratha, Swadeshi Pizza, Moradabadi Dal, Udupi Spa Dosa
description:
ITO is a bustling hub of administration, commerce, and education in Delhi, recently became the backdrop for our food tour. Accompanied by our physician friend from MAMC, Akshat, we set out to explore the culinary gems of this vibrant neighborhood.  

We began at Yadav Nariyal Pani Bhandar, where we sipped on refreshing ripe coconut water. The young seller told us how the cart has been around for years, with the coconut pulp sold at traffic crossings while the water is served fresh here. It was the perfect start to our journey.  

At Hum Hindustani on Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, we stepped into what felt like a cosy co-working space where one could work while enjoying their favorite food. A true landmark of Ito’s culinary scene, we indulged in a posi dosa and chow chow bhaat. The flavors were bold, comforting, and deliciously authentic.  

On Vishnu Digamber Marg, we stopped for a Swadeshi Pizza for Moong Dal Pizza, essentially a moonglet with pizza toppings. The unique combination of textures and flavors made it a surprisingly delightful experience. We also sampled Muradabad dal here, a comforting yet zesty lentil based dish. 

Next, we tried a slightly different version of dabeli at the Bombay Special Food Stall near ESIC. The aalu masala inside was quite flavourful, setting this version apart from the usual.  

We ended our journey at Sardar Ji Parathe Wale near ITO Metro Gate No. 4. Run by a hardworking and genial Sardarji, the place offered freshly prepared parathas with a variety of curries. We opted for their anda paratha, a hearty creation combining aloo paratha with beaten egg stuffed inside. Watching it being made right in front of us was as enjoyable as eating it.  

This food tour through ITO gave us a taste of its vibrant culinary culture, blending traditional flavors with innovative twists.

Narr.. poor Santosh is making bread in the factory till late night when the set comes to him.

Seth becomes normal and asks.... Santosh, all the goods are ready, right, because the bread packets have to be delivered early tomorrow morning.

Santosh getting tired... yes set... I have prepared all the bread packets.

Natr.. just then there is a sound of lightning in the sky which Santosh hears.

Santosh asks worriedly... set, is it raining outside? How loudly is the lightning flashing?

Seth Nirmal... yes, the weather is bad outside. You leave for home quickly and take this, your daily wages for today and this ₹50 extra for your overtime.

Narr.  ₹50 for the factory set might have been a small amount but for Santosh, who was a poor bread earner, ₹50 was very valuable at that time because the condition of his house was very bad due to the rains and he had to run his family at any cost.

Santosh happily says /...Thank you very much Seth, I am leaving.

Narr.=Seth gives him a packet of bread.

Set Nirmal...Take this packet of bread too, your children will eat it.

Narr.. As soon as he comes out of the factory with bread and money, it is rainy weather and there is heavy lightning.

Santosh worries..Today it is such a rainy weather, it will rain very heavily, I should leave for home quickly, otherwise if I get drenched in the rain, these breads will also get spoiled.

Narrtion..Santosh starts moving towards home quickly, then it starts raining very hard and a storm starts hitting the stove.  Rita, sitting in front, was looking towards the door again and again with the hope of ration being brought. Paras, writhing with hunger, asks for food.

Paras crying... Mummy, Mummy, I am very hungry, my stomach is also aching, please give me something to eat, huhu huh.

Khushi... crying... Yes Mummy, if you have rotis from last night, then give it to me with salt and oil, we will eat.

Narr... Seeing both the children writhing with hunger and asking for dry roti, the poor daughter-in-law's heart almost breaks because the other days they used to show tantrums in eating dal rice, now both were ready to eat dry roti because the family had not cooked food for the whole day.. Just then, Santosh, drenched in rain, comes inside with little ration in a bag.


Paras happily says, Mummy, Mummy, look, Papa has come with the ration, cook food quickly.

Santosh gives the ration, take this, Rita, I have brought ration for two times, today the owner has given me ₹50 extra for overtime, so I have brought a packet of milk, please make some tea.

Rita, I will make it now.

Shanti cares, daughter-in-law, leave everything, first ask about his head and apply oil, see, he has come completely drenched in the rain, the rains of Sawan and Bhado are very bad, if it catches cold fever, it does not go away easily.

Nat.  Rita brings a towel and quickly dries Santosh's head and applies mustard oil. Then both the children stare at the bread packet with hungry eyes.

Tears in Paras' eyes.. Mummy, Mummy, are you very hungry? Should I take out one bread from the packet and eat it?

Mother-in-law gets emotional.. Oh my dear grandson, take not one but two breads and eat them. You are hungry.. right?

Paras gets happy.. Okay grandma..., here Khushi Didi, you also eat bread, you have not eaten anything either.

Nart.. Paras takes two breads for himself and gives it to his sister as well. Although everyone was hungry, both the children start eating the bread by folding it. Shanti's eyes fill up.

Shanti cries.. Will this bread fill the stomach of both of you? Nibha go daughter, put the dal bhaat to cook.. See how both are eating the bread by cutting it.. Neither of them has eaten a grain of food since morning. If you eat too much refined flour, it will harm your stomach. 

Narr... Nibha quickly comes to the kitchen where the lack of living in poverty was clearly visible in the empty ration boxes. While on one hand the rich eat good food in the rainy season, the same rain makes the poor family dependent even for two meals a day... Due to less ration, Nibha cooks half rice and a handful of dal.

Nibha...helplessly asks, mother what vegetables should I cut. There is no vegetable at all.

Rita...helplessly... Nibha see, there must be two-four potatoes

title: Nehlle Pe Dehlla 4K Full Movie | Saif Ali Khan & Bipasha Basu | Sanjay Dutt & Kim Sharma | Comedy
description:
Nehlle Pe Dehlla is a hilarious Bollywood thriller comedy film that was released in 2007. This film has been directed by Ajay Chandhok and the catchy dialogues have been written by Rumi Jaffrey. Sanjay Dutt, Saif Ali Khan, Bipasha Basu have lead roles in the film.


नेहले पे देहला बॉलीवुड की जबरदस्त थ्रिलर कॉमेडी फिल्म है, जिसे 2007  में रिलीज किया गया था। इस फिल्म को डायरेक्टर अजय चन्दोक ने किया है और कैची डायलॉग रूमी जाफ़री ने लिखा है। फिल्म में संजय दत्त, सैफ अली खान, बिपाशा बासु का लीड रोल है। 

कहानी दो चोर जिम्मी (सैफ अली खान) और जॉनी (संजय दत्त ) अमीर बनने का सपना देखते हैं और एक होटल मैनेजर   बलराम साहनी (शक्ति कपूर ) को ब्लैकमेल करने का फैसला करते हैं, जो अपने ही होटल से पैसे चुराता है। किसी और से पहले - अकाउंट्स, फाइनेंस डिपार्टमेंट, यहां तक   कि सीसीटीवी भी - जिम्मी और जॉनी इसका पता लगा लेते हैं और उसी होटल में वेटर के भेष में वहां काम करके बलराम को ब्लैकमेल करने का फैसला करते हैं। जब तक वो जिम्मी और जॉनी अपने काम को अज़ाम देते उससे पहले ही बलराम की हत्या हो जाती है। 

अब, जिमी और जॉनी को सबको यह दिखाना है कि बलराम ज़िंदा है, ताकि वे अपना पैसा पा सकें। इसलिए, वे एक मृत शरीर से हर संभव काम करवाते हैं जो आपकी कल्पना से परे है। लाश संगीत पर नाचती है, कार चलाती है, अपने बैंक को ऑपरेट भी करता है..भला मरा हुआ आदमी से जिम्मी और जॉनी ये सारे काम कैसे करवाते है? ये जानने के लिए देखिय़े जबरदस्त कॉमेडी से भरपूर फिल्म 'नेहले पे देहला'

title: 🍴 Italian BYOB in Amritsar 😍😍 | Rs 50 ke Chips Rs 150 me 🤩🤩
description:
Amritsar never fails to surprise us with its amazing street food, and today we bring you something truly unique — Italian BYOB (Build Your Own Bowl) at just ₹150! 🤩🔥

This young and handsome boy has created a food trend that’s winning everyone’s hearts ❤️. Let’s take you step by step through this delicious journey:

🥗 Step 1: The Fresh Salad
He starts by taking a round utensil and adds freshly cut salad 🥒🍅🥕 that is already prepared with multiple veggies. It’s a healthy and colorful base that makes the bowl fresh and crunchy! 😍

🧀 Step 2: The Special Paneer
Next comes the star ingredient — marinated cheese paneer! 🧀✨
The best part? It’s pure dairy paneer, not soya paneer ❌. The marination adds an Italian twist that makes the flavor absolutely mouthwatering 🤤.

🌶️ Step 3: Seasonings & Sauces
Now, he sprinkles seasoning, chili flakes 🌶️, and their secret special sauce 🍯. The aroma itself will make you hungry instantly! He mixes everything really well so that each bite is packed with flavor 😋.

🍟 Step 4: The Crunch Factor
Here’s the most exciting part — he opens a packet of chips! 🥳
Whether it’s Doritos, Lays, or other chips, it’s completely your choice 😍. For this bowl, he picks Doritos, crushes the entire packet inside the mix, and blends it all together for that perfect crispy texture 🤩🔥.

🥡 Step 5: Packing the Magic
After mixing, the crunchy-cheesy salad is packed back into a chip packet! Yes, you read that right 🤯. Then he adds more sauces on top and gives it another good mix so that every bite is creamy, cheesy, and crunchy all at once 😍🤤.

🎉 The Final BYOB
And finally… your Italian BYOB is ready! 😍💥
Crispy chips, fresh salad, marinated paneer, and flavorful sauces all come together to make a snack that looks amazing and tastes even better 🤩.

If you’re in Amritsar, this pocket-friendly delight at just ₹150 is a must-try! 🙌💯

✅ Unique Italian twist in Indian street food 🇮🇳🇮🇹
✅ Fresh paneer & veggies 🥗
✅ Your choice of chips 🍟
✅ Budget-friendly & filling 🤩
✅ Perfect for foodies who love experimenting ❤️

title: Ballimaran Nahari Shaheen Bagh | Complete Recipe Of Ballimaran Nihari | Globalecentre Delhi Nahari
description:
Ballimaran Nahari Shaheen Bagh is the only Nahari specific brand that has multiple branches in many cities in India. Ballimaran Nahari complete recipe is what you will see in this video.
We spent whole day at Ballimaran Nahari Restaurant Shaheen Bagh and shot the Nahari making from scratch till end.
Gloablecentre Nahari videos are the ones that you all love to watch.

I shot complete recipe while making it live at BALLIMARAN NAHARI Shaheen Bagh Delhi. Ballimaran Nahari is the only Nahari specific chain in India serving in more than 15 major cities in India.

Introduction of Nahari
Nahari is a traditional dish that started during the Mughal era in Old Delhi. It was eaten by royal families for breakfast, especially in winter.

The word Nahari comes from the Arabic word Nahari, meaning “day,” because it was eaten early in the morning. The dish is made by slow-cooking meat (usually buffalo meat or mutton) overnight with spices like cloves, cardamom, and black pepper. It becomes soft, spicy, and full of flavor.

In Old Delhi, Nahari became popular among workers and common people too, giving them strength for the whole day. Even today, shops in areas like Jama Masjid and Chitli Qabar are famous for their tasty Nahari, served with naan or khameeri roti.

Ludhiana, the industrial heart of Punjab, is just as rich in flavor as it is in industry, thanks to its vibrant street food scene. The city’s bustling markets and food stalls offer a delicious variety of Punjabi delights that cater to every palate. From the spicy chole bhature served piping hot with tangy pickles to the crisp and flavorful aloo tikki chaat, Ludhiana’s streets are a haven for food lovers. One cannot miss the iconic paneer pakoras, deep-fried to golden perfection, or the beloved tandoori parathas served with creamy lassi. Local favorites like kulcha chole and rajma chawal from roadside dhabas reflect the true essence of Punjabi comfort food. Whether it's day or night, the aroma of sizzling spices and freshly made dishes fills the air, making Ludhiana a must-visit destination for anyone who wants to experience authentic North Indian street food.

title: Mussoorie Tourist Places | Mussoorie Best Places to Visit | Travel Vlogs in India | EP-1
description:
Mussoorie Tourist Places | Mussoorie Best Places to Visit | Travel Vlogs in India | EP-1


Planning a Mussoorie trip from Delhi in 2026? In this detailed Mussoorie vlog, we take you through a full 2-day Mussoorie itinerary, travel cost (in Indian rupees), transport options, hotel details, local food reviews, and the best places to visit in Mussoorie for couples, families, or friends.

Our journey began with an AC sleeper bus from Delhi to Dehradun that cost us just ₹600 per person. From Dehradun, we took a cab to Mussoorie for ₹1,000. For budget travelers, we share a cheaper way to reach Mussoorie—just ₹80 by bus from Dehradun Railway Station.

We explored Mussoorie on a rented motorbike and shared detailed prices for scooty rentals, taxi rates, and parking costs so you can plan your own trip easily.

🚩 Mussoorie Day 1 Itinerary:

Our first stop was Lal Tibba in Landour, one of the highest viewpoints in Mussoorie. We reached via motorbike and paid ₹50 for scooty parking. Opposite Lal Tibba, we visited Savoy Cafe, had delicious pizza and lime soda with a scenic mountain view. The total cost was ₹700. We shared the complete restaurant review and menu so you can decide if it’s worth it.

Next, we headed to the famous Bhatta Falls, where we relaxed by the waterfall and enjoyed tea, coffee, lime soda, omelet, and Maggi. You can also try adventure activities like ziplining, giant swing, and rope cycling at Bhatta Adventure Park. We shared the entry fee (₹80), parking charges (₹30 for scooty, ₹100 for car), and ropeway ticket cost (₹150 one side, ₹250 both sides). If you use the ropeway, the park entry is free.

In the evening, we trekked to Dalai Hills, a hidden gem for sunset lovers. The trek takes 15–20 mins, and there’s no entry fee. You’ll see a stunning Buddha statue, colorful prayer flags, and panoramic sunset views.

At night, we explored Mussoorie Mall Road, tried local street food, and had dinner at Maharaja Palace, where we ordered butter chicken and naan. We shared our full food review, taste, and cost details.

🏨 Hotel Stay in Mussoorie:

We stayed just 500 meters from Mall Road at Hotel City Castle, which cost ₹1,200 per night, including breakfast. The hotel has parking space and is suitable for couples/families. We also gave a complete room tour in the video to help you decide if it’s worth booking.

🚩 Mussoorie Day 2 Itinerary:

We started the day by visiting George Everest Peak, the highest point in Mussoorie, with stunning hill views and beautiful roads for bikers and photographers.

Next, you can visit the iconic Kempty Falls, where you can swim or take a ropeway ride. We explained the ropeway cost, entry, and food options around the falls.

We then visited the Mussoorie Lake, one of the most popular tourist spots. There’s a ₹30 entry fee, and parking was free for us (two-wheeler). At Mussoorie Lake, you can enjoy paragliding (₹1,500), boating, water ball, haunted house, ziplining, and giant swing. We shared the price list of all adventure activities. We also had lunch overlooking the Doon Valley—a must-do for scenic views while eating.

In the evening, you can end your trip by visiting Gun Hill, where you can either trek or take a ropeway to the top. It offers panoramic views of the Himalayas and Mall Road.

🎒 Whether you’re planning a 2-day weekend trip to Mussoorie or a longer stay, this video covers:
 • Mussoorie itinerary for couples/families
 • Transport from Delhi to Dehradun to Mussoorie
 • Motorbike rental and taxi fare in Mussoorie
 • Best restaurants and local food options
 • Adventure activities at Bhatta Falls & Mussoorie Lake
 • Hidden spots like Dalai Hills and George Everest Peak
 • Mussoorie hotel near Mall Road with parking
 • Ropeway costs, parking charges, and full budget breakdown

📍If you’re planning a Delhi to Mussoorie trip, this vlog will help you plan your route, budget, stay, and must-visit places with real prices and travel tips.

title: Basukinath to Deoghar via Trikut Parvat + Huge Peda Factory @ Ghormara + Samosi + Shringar/Aarti
description:
In this episode, we begin our journey from the sacred grounds of Baba Basukinath Temple, located around 45 km from Deoghar. Considered a key part of the pilgrimage circuit, the temple is visited by thousands of devotees every day, especially during the Shravani Mela. As we arrived, we were guided by a panda (temple priest), who helped us through the rituals. He performed a brief pooja and handed Anubhav a pot of holy water, which he carried into the sanctum to offer to the deity. The atmosphere was intense, a sea of devotees, chants echoing in the background, and a current of energy that made the experience unforgettable.

After the darshan, we wandered into the narrow bylanes surrounding the temple, known locally as Peda Gali. Lined with sweet shops and the aroma of khoya wafting through the air, it reminded us of the iconic peda gali near Baba Baidyanath Dham. Though smaller in scale, it had the same charm, people calling out their specialties, trays of fresh peda, and that old-town warmth.

Next, we started our street food trail with a stop at Marwari Basa, a simple eatery that serves both snacks and home-style meals. We opted for a plate of rice and dal, light, nourishing, and served with that unmistakable hospitality that small-town kitchens are known for.

Our food trail continued as we headed to Ghormara, a small town known for its legendary peda. Our destination was Sukhari Mandal Peda, believed to be the oldest peda shop in the area. The owner welcomed us warmly, shared the story of the shop, and even walked us through the peda-making process- boiling the milk, stirring the khoya, and shaping the peda by hand. We tasted it fresh, soft, milky, and gently sweet. A quiet moment of indulgence.

Just outside, we spotted a bhunja cart, run by a young man who kept his space remarkably neat. The mix of roasted grains, peanuts, and spices made for a crunchy, flavorful snack. We washed it down with a hot cup of chai from a nearby stall, a comforting pause in our journey.

From there, we made our way to Trikut Parvat, a scenic spot about 15 km from Deoghar. The hill is associated with mythology and is believed to be the meeting point of the three major Hindu deities, Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh. Though the ropeway was closed due to maintenance, the view of the hills and surrounding greenery offered a moment of calm after the hustle of the temples and markets.

As evening approached, we returned to Baba Baidyanath Dham for the Sandhya Aarti. Before entering, we stopped at the famous Dukhi Shah Dukan to try the Muni Samosa. Crisp on the outside, with a well-spiced potato filling, it was one of the best samosas we have had on this journey.

The episode closes with the powerful experience of Sandhya Aarti. It was a fitting end to a day filled with devotion, stories and simple food.

I spent the day trying three very different biryanis across Delhi, each at a completely different price point. The contrast in techniques, textures and aromas made the journey even more fun.

The final tasting was the legendary Dum Pukht experience at ITC Maurya where subtle aromas, beautifully cooked lamb and moist long-grain rice created a refined and memorable finish. Delhi really does have biryani for every craving.

Moti Mahal ne hi isse duniya ko diya, aur yeh ab global superstar hai. Thodi si makhani richness aur desi swad ka perfect balance—yeh sirf khana nahi, ek love story hai jo yahin se shuru hui!

Tandoori Chicken: Smoky, juicy, aur masaledar! Tandoor mein pakaya hua yeh chicken, yogurt aur spices ke marinade ke saath, ek char-grilled magic deta hai. Har bite mein crispy edges aur succulent meat ka maza—party ka hero!

Mutton Burra: Yeh hai mutton ka badshah! Spicy, succulent, aur tandoor mein perfectly charred, iske bold flavors aur tender texture aapko seedha Punjab ke dhabe pe le jayenge. Thoda wild, thoda intense—non-veg lovers ka ultimate crush!
Butter Chicken ko thoda alag isliye kehte hain kyunki yeh Moti Mahal ka original creation hai—ek aisa dish jo 1940s mein yahin paida hua aur aaj duniya bhar mein Indian cuisine ka naam roshan karta hai. Iska silky gravy aur mild flavors isse har kisi ka favorite banate hain, chahe woh desi ho ya videshi!

title: Massive Baripada Evening Food Tour | Dahi Aalu + Guda Ladoo + Steamed Sandesh + Anda Tadka
description:
This episode is an immersive evening food tour in Baripada, led by our host Akash, a local who is deeply knowledgeable about the city’s heritage and culinary landscape.

We began our journey at Barik Tea Stall, fondly called BTS by locals, inspired by the Korean band due to its abbreviation. The coal oven here has a unique contraption that helps fan the fire efficiently. Akash has been coming here for the past 12 years. It is a popular spot for khatti, where people gather over tea and conversations. We also found a variety of cookies and snacks to go along with the tea.

Next, we visited Nini Bhai’s Dahi Aalu stall in Rathapadia, which has been around for nearly 40 years. Their signature dish, dahi aalu, is a tangy and comforting preparation of potatoes and curd with a perfect balance of spices. We also tried aalu dum, which was rich and flavourful, matar aalu kasa with its bold and spicy notes, and masala mudhi, a staple snack that is light, crunchy and deeply satisfying. Akash’s insights made the experience even richer.

We then headed to Jay Bajrang Guda Laddu, where we were joined by Mona. Here, we tried arisa pitha and the famous Baripada guda laddu. Guda laddu holds special significance as a key prasad during the Rath Yatra in Baripada. It has a unique texture with a slight caramelised sweetness, enhanced with subtle spices.

We made a short visit to the Baripada night market, which interestingly was once a Central Jail. From there, we went to Bapa Jhiya Jalakhia Dokan, a bustling fried snacks cart run by a father-daughter duo. We had masala mudhi and freshly fried chana dal fritters, which were crisp and flavourful. We also tried their special anda chop, a batter-coated egg snack topped with onions. It was a fun and indulgent evening bite.

Next, we stopped for some soda. The owner was warm and friendly, and we shared some great conversations filled with laughter. These small moments added so much warmth to the journey.

We then visited SSS Sweets to try their speciality, chhena poda. It was soft, caramelised and rich in flavour. We tried two variants and enjoyed both.

After this, we stopped at a crowded roadside anda ghugni stall. The ghugni topped with boiled eggs made for a wholesome and satisfying meal. The crowd itself spoke about its popularity.

Akash then took us to Babu Bhai’s shop to try punti kassa and other offal-based dishes. These are bold, masala-rich preparations and definitely an acquired taste. Locals love to enjoy them with mudhi.

Our next stop was Gajanan Vilas, known for its wide variety of sweets. We tried Mona ji’s favourite steamed sandesh and a malai roll. Both were light, fresh and delicately sweet.

We then visited Maguni Mixture, an old and famous namkeen shop that continues to draw huge crowds. We tried a few snacks and also got some packed. Both Akash and Mona have been coming here since childhood, which made it even more special.

Next, we headed to Kala Dhaba to try a unique combination of rice flour roti and country chicken kassa. It is a busy place and the rotis need to be pre-ordered as they are made in limited batches. The rotis were soft and paired beautifully with the rich, spicy chicken.

Our last stop for the day was Hotel Neelkamal. Here, we tried their anda tadka with mutton curry and a special chickpea-based starter. The flavours were bold, comforting and deeply satisfying. It is a favourite highway dhaba for many, and we could see why.

This evening in Baripada was not just about food. It was about people, stories, memories and discovering a city through its flavours. A heartfelt thank you to Akash and Mona for making this journey so special.

This is a mini food vlog of my recent visit to Delhi’s famous Sarojini Nagar Market. Sarojini Nagar is one of the most famous markets in Delhi and it is well known for its variety of cheap clothes, jewellery, electronics and more. Although, other than shopping, Sarojini Nagar market is always famous for the delicious street food that is available at every corner of this market. title: Old Delhi Street Food Tour | Purani Dilli ke Pakwaan | Ashok & Ashok Meat Dhaba|Bedmi Puri |Biryani
description:
Join Kunal Vijayakar in this mouth-watering episode of Khaane Mein Kya Hai, as he embarks on a flavorful journey through the heart of Old Delhi, discovering the city's iconic street food spots! From hidden gems to centuries-old food traditions, Kunal explores the best of Delhi’s street food culture.
Kunal kicks things off in Chandni Chowk, visiting Jain Pavitra Chach Bhandar for a comforting plate of homemade bread butter and a refreshing glass of chach.
- Next, he heads to Chawri Bazaar's Shyam Sweets to try their legendary Bedmi Puri with Aloo Sabzi — a must-try combo for all street food lovers.
- Kunal then takes a trip to Daulat Ki Chaat, an exquisite dessert that’s often compared to Malaiyo—a creamy, frothy delight that will leave you wanting more.
- Heading to Saddar Bazaar, Kunal indulges in the famous mutton and chicken preparations from Ashok & Ashok, a local favorite for tender, flavorful meats.
- To wrap things up, he makes his way to the historic Jama Masjid, where he tries the famous biryani prepared by none other than Kallan Bawarchi, a legendary name in Old Delhi’s biryani scene.

Don’t miss out on this gastronomic adventure through Old Delhi's narrow lanes and timeless flavors!

title: Kitne Kha Loge ?? 📌 Odean Sweets Delhi #gulabjamun #foodkars
Ep 10, MALKA GANJ Street Food Walk I Rawalpindi Chole Bhature + Authority Keema Meat + Chicken Tawa
description:
0:90-0:51 
0:52-4:17 BANSHI DI HATTI
4:18-8:26 VED DHABA
8:27-10.49 MANOHAR MATTHI 
10:50-15:19 GULLU'S
15:20-21:00 CORNER WALI MATTHI SHOP
21:01- 25:20 BABLU SNACKS
25:21-26:55 BIKANER SWEET CENTER


In today’s episode of Delhi Neighbourhood Eats, we take you through the best of Malka Ganj’s street food delights!  

We began our food tour at Banshi Di Hatti, a beloved spot run by the third generation of the family. Known for their chole bhature, they serve a unique twist with bhature stuffed with aloo or paneer. It’s a treat you simply can’t miss.  

Next, we visited Ved Dhaba on Chandrawal Road, a place Anubhav frequented during his hostel days. Famous among locals and students, their menu includes fresh and hygienic options like chana dal, rajma, butter paneer masala, and tandoori roti. We also tried their signature sweet matka malai toast, which was delightful.  

Manohar Matthi Wala, also on Chandrawal Road, was our next stop. Known for their savory snacks, especially matthi, they offer a wide variety of options. We tried their healthy matthi and couldn’t resist picking up an assorted snacks box for later.  

At Gullu’s, opposite the Malka Ganj bus stop, we experienced a legacy that started with simple dishes outside the State Transport Authority office. Today, they serve a range of delicious fares. We picked up our order here and enjoyed their rich and robust mutton keema with soft, fresh roti.  

The Corner Wali Matthi Shop on Chandrawal Road is Anubhav’s favourite spot for mathi. We spoke to the current owner, who shared the shop’s legacy, and then indulged in some of their most popular snacks with a cup of chai. As always, everything was fresh and delicious.  

Bablu Snacks near Ghanta Ghar was our next destination. Famous for their extensive tawa menu, we ordered the chicken tikka tawa masala. The chicken tikka, tossed in a flavorful gravy, was an absolute delight.  

Our final stop was Bikaner Sweet Center near Ghanta Ghar, where we ended the tour on a sweet note with moong dal halwa and gajar ka halwa. Both desserts were rich, warm, and the perfect conclusion to a memorable food tour in Malka Ganj.

title: EP01 Hyderabad to Nagpur by Road | Scenic Views, Local Food & Surprises! I Bharat Ghoomo I
description:
Join us on an unforgettable family road trip from Hyderabad to Nagpur, covering approximately 520 km in 9 hours! 🚗💨

We—two adults and our energetic 8-year-old explorer—set off at 6 AM, embarking on a scenic journey through the heart of Telangana and Maharashtra. Our route took us through:

Hyderabad → Medchal → Manoharabad → Tupran → Ramayampet → Bhiknoor → Kamareddy → Indalwai → Nizamabad → Armur → Nirmal → Ichoda → Adilabad → Pandharkadwa → Khatara → Wadki → Hinganghat → Patanbori → Nagpur

🌄 Highlights of the Journey:

A peaceful breakfast stop near Armur, nestled in the forests of Telangana, where we relished Idli, Dosa, Puri, and Wadas

Crossing the majestic Godavari River, soaking in the natural beauty 🌊

Refreshing sugarcane juice pit stop 🍹

Multiple police checks due to election season 🚨

A hearty Punjabi lunch at Sher-e-Punjab Hotel after entering Maharashtra—Dal Tadka and Tandoori Rotis that hit the spot! 🍽️

A couple of unexpected flat tyres and quick repairs that added a dash of adventure to our day 🛞🔧

Finally arriving at the elegant Le Meridien Nagpur for a well-deserved rest 🏨✨

This video captures the essence of Indian road travel—the food, the landscapes, the surprises, and the joy of exploring together as a family. Whether you're planning a similar trip or just love travel stories, this one's for you!

description:
ICONIC Food Places in Delhi | Bhogal's CHHOLE Bathure, Special Rajmah Chawal, Dosa | Indian Food

1st Location - Bhogal's Chhole Bathure, Atul Grove Road, Janpath, Connaught Place, Delhi

2nd Google - Dhaba Food, Near Shankar Market, Connaught Place, Delhi

3rd Location- Kutty's South Indian Food, Janpath, Connaught Place, Delhi

Delhi, the capital of India, is famous for its vibrant culture, historical landmarks, and diverse street food scene. Whether you're exploring its bustling markets or iconic monuments, there's a lot to see and experience.

Chhole Bhature is one of North India's most beloved dishes, a hearty and flavorful combination of spicy chickpea curry (chhole) and deep-fried fluffy bread (bhature). It's a must-try for anyone exploring Indian cuisine, especially if you're visiting Delhi or Punjab.

Delhi's dhaba food offers an authentic taste of North Indian cuisine, blending rustic flavors with hearty portions. Dhabas are roadside eateries that serve delicious and affordable meals, often cooked with traditional techniques that enhance the flavors.

Rajma Chawal is a beloved North Indian comfort food that pairs spiced kidney bean curry (rajma) with steamed rice (chawal). It's hearty, flavorful, and often associated with home-style cooking. In Delhi, you’ll find this dish served in homes, street-side eateries, and even upscale restaurants, but the best experience is often at roadside dhabas.

Butter Masala Dosa is a delicious twist on the classic South Indian masala dosa, enhanced with a generous dollop of butter for extra richness and flavor. This crispy, golden-brown crepe made from fermented rice and lentil batter is stuffed with a spiced potato filling and served with a variety of chutneys and sambar (a tangy lentil soup).

Rava Kesari is a classic South Indian dessert made from semolina (rava/suji), sugar, ghee, and flavored with saffron and cardamom. It’s a popular dish often prepared during festivals, special occasions, or as a quick treat. Known for its vibrant orange color and melt-in-the-mouth texture, Rava Kesari is simple yet incredibly flavorful.

title: Best KASOL Food Walk l Hemp Coffee + Hummus + Shakshuka + Falafel King + German Bakery + Shambu Momo
description:
Join us on a vibrant food walk through Kasol as we explore some of the most loved cafes and hidden gems in the area. Hosted by Anubhav Sapra and Khushboo Barry, this trail is packed with stories, flavours, and memorable conversations.

We began at The Evergreen on Manikaran Road near the Forest Rest House, where we met Jatin Sharma and Tal Gross. Their combo crispy chicken platter was a mountain feast layered with bold Middle Eastern flavours-crispy schnitzel, creamy labneh, comforting shakshuka, fresh salad, French fries, and warm naan, all brought together with a drizzle of tahini and chilli garlic sauce. Hearty, wholesome, and deeply satisfying.

Next stop was King Falafel near Nature Park. Their signature falafel, paired with hummus, tahini, laffa, and fries, was a pocket-sized powerhouse of texture and taste-crunchy, fluffy, spiced, and truly heart warming.

At Little Italy Inn on Manikaran Road, we met Vanita and tried their farmhouse pizza loaded with fresh toppings and gooey cheese, followed by a balanced, creamy tiramisu. We also spoke to the young owner, who shared how her parents started the cafe, turning it into a beloved spot over the years.

We dropped by Offlimits Cafe, India’s first hemp cafe, where we met one of the young co-founders, Mayank. Hemp is native to this region, and that’s what inspired them to reimagine it in the culinary space. This unique cafe blends locally sourced produce with hemp-based ingredients in a contemporary setting. It’s a refreshing, offbeat stop for anyone looking to explore alternative, mindful food options.

At German Bakery, Balram treated us to a soft, flaky croissant and a decadent cream cheesecake. We chatted about the legacy of German bakery their evolution across India, and how each carries a unique local story while maintaining their classic charm.

In Nature Park, Shambhu Momo served us piping hot chicken momos, thanks to Sunil. Juicy, flavour-packed, and just the kind of snack you crave in the chilly mountain breeze.

Moon Dance Cafe, near the bridge, was another memorable stop. Their red and white sauce pastas were comforting, the trout fresh from local streams, and the biryani rich with warm spices. We later returned to try their spaghetti pasta - light, flavourful, and indulgent. With its laid-back vibe, artistic interiors, and garden seating, Moon Dance is a soulful cafe that invites you to linger.

This food trail through Kasol is more than just meals, it’s a journey across forest trails, cozy cafes, warm kitchens, and a melting pot of global and local tastes. Watch the full episode to soak it all in.

Welcome back to the channel, food lovers! In this video, we take you on a flavorful journey to the streets of Delhi, where a street vendor showcases the art of making real, healthy, street-style tomato soup in MASSIVE quantities! 🍜

Delhi winters and a hot cup of tomato soup go hand in hand, and nothing beats the rich, tangy, spicy, and buttery street version made live on a big tawa with love and flair. This is not just soup; it's a warm hug in a bowl! 😍

Watch as bhaiya starts with fresh, juicy tomatoes that are pressure cooked until soft. Then comes the exciting part – blending the boiled tomatoes into a rich pulp, which is then poured into a hot, butter-laden pan. Spices like black pepper, salt, red chilli powder, chaat masala, and secret masalas are added to give that authentic desi tang. A dash of sugar balances the acidity while cornflour slurry gives it that smooth, thick consistency. 🥄

To finish it off, bhaiya adds cubes of butter, a generous handful of chopped coriander, and crunchy croutons for texture. The aroma that fills the air is absolutely divine – a blend of tomato richness and street-style spice that warms your soul instantly. This is what real Delhi-style tomato soup is all about – wholesome, healthy, spicy, and full of love. ❤️

If you enjoy watching authentic Indian street food preparation, this video will keep you hooked from start to finish. Perfect for soup lovers, foodies, and anyone who wants to relive the taste of Delhi’s winter evenings.

title: Ep - 14, Delhi’s Best DAL @ Sialkot Dhaba + Gabbar/Gabbi Kadi Chawal l Multani Moth Kachori + Chaap
description:
We went on a street food tour in Geeta Colony with our host Rishabh Bhatia, a young man who knows the food scene of East Delhi like the back of his hand. With a friendly smile and a clear passion for the local food culture, he walked us through lanes lined with food joints that have stood the test of time and tastes.

Our first stop was Gabbar Kadhi Chawal, a small outlet with a quirky name that serves up what might just be one of the best plates of rajma kadhi chawal in the city. You can go for either rajma chawal, kadhi chawal, or a mix of both. We chose the mix and were greeted with thick, flavorful curries poured over rice—simple, hearty, and deeply satisfying.

Next, we made our way to Nagpal Di Hatti for their quintessential Multani moth kachori. Here, khasta moong dal kachoris are served with thick moth ki dal, mixed with a special spice blend and chutneys, and topped with a small amount of rice. The magic lies in the Multani masala that elevates the dish with its bold and earthy punch. Rishabh showed us how he enjoys it best—by crushing the kachoris into the dal, letting the flavors meld into one soul-satisfying bowl.

At Yellow Bowl, we were greeted with a menu full of playful names and wild combinations. Known for their variety of chaap and momos, we picked their Naughty Momo, Cheese Corn Momo, and Punjabi Chaap after a fun chat with the owner. It was a youthful, experimental spot with food that matched its energy—bold, cheesy, and crowd-pleasing.

We took a breather at a cozy little cafe called Piyega The Coffee Co. It’s a snug hideout offering a mix of classic and fusion coffees. We tried their Irish Blonde and Italiana Tiramisu, both served in stylish cups, balancing strong coffee notes with sweet, dessert-like tones.

Our next stop was Ramesh Vaishno Dhaba, a place that celebrates East Delhi’s deep love for chaap. The variety here was astounding, and the aroma coming from their butter-laden dishes was irresistible. On Rishabh’s recommendation, we tried the stuffed chaap, pudina chaap, tawa chaap, and a fantastic pyaaz roti. The stuffed chaap, dunked in butter, was the bestseller for a reason—rich, spicy, and absolutely addictive. The pyaaz roti, packed with generous bits of onion and baked in a tandoor, was a great companion to the chaap.

One of the most heartfelt stops was Pyarelal Sialkot Vegetarian. This place has been part of Rishabh’s childhood, and he recalled fondly how the owner would always hand out candies to kids, a gesture of warmth that stayed with him over the years. We sat down to try their slow-cooked dal makhani and paneer lababdar with rotis. The dal, cooked for around nine hours, was creamy, luxurious, and comforting—truly a dish that felt like a hug.

We ended the tour at Gogia Shudh Khoya & Paneer Bhandar with something sweet. Here, we tried their jalebi, rabri, and kulhad doodh. The jalebis were crisp and syrupy, the rabri was thick and luscious, and the kulhad doodh had that smoky, earthy flavor that only clay cups can lend. It was the perfect ending to a walk that was not just about food, but memories, stories, and the unmistakable warmth of Delhi’s streets.

Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah is a comedy show inspired by the famous humorous column 'Duniya Ne Undha Chashmah' written by the eminent Gujarati writer Mr. Tarak Mehta. This show revolves around the Gada Family which consists of uneducated businessmen Jethalal Champaklal Gada, Jethalal’s Wife Daya & their naughty Son Tipendra Gada living in 'Gokuldham Co-operative Society' and covers topical issues which are socially relevant. In case of a problem and emergency, Jethalal Gada often rushes to Taarak Mehta to seek his help and guidance as he finds a philosopher in him. The residents of the housing society, help each other find solutions when they face common, real-life challenges and get involved in sticky situations.

Narr... A cool breeze is blowing, and the weather is foggy all around. Inside a dense forest, daughters-in-law are picking greens from the fields.

Kusum21... Happy... Sister-in-law, this time our field has produced such wonderful cholai mustard spinach. And the fastest growing is this Bathua green... And the real fun of eating greens comes in the cold weather.

Narr... Saying this, Kusum, shivering in the cold, digs up the greens from the field bed and puts them in a basket. Meanwhile, Nupur uproots the spinach along with its roots.

Babita22... Getting a little serious... Nupur, what have you done? You uprooted the entire greens along with the roots. Hey, greens are not plucked like this; only the leaves are picked, and the stalk is left so that the greens can grow again.

Nupur19... Normal... Huhu Huuu Babita Bhabhi, I was just picking spinach leaves, and by mistake, I uprooted one of our plants.  The spinach plant was damaged.

Natr... Just then, Babita devised a solution and planted the spinach plant in the ground by digging the soil deep with a hoe. Due to the cold weather, the entire field was filled with fog. Champa and Madhavi were cooking food by setting up a stove a short distance away from the field when suddenly, an injured bull came roaring from the forest and came into their field and started growling at the three of them.

The bull growled, "Huuhu Huuu"

Nar... Seeing such a large bull in front of them, the three of them stood there in fear. Would these daughters-in-law be able to defend themselves? But the question is, why are these five daughters-in-law living in such a dense forest in such bitterly cold weather? To understand the root of the matter, let's start from the beginning.

Flashback
Nqrr... where old Dinesh is sitting on a cot, shivering in the cold.

Dinesh 50... Shivering, "Huuhu Huuh"  Huh... Hey brother, will anyone give me some tea today? I've been sitting on this cot for the last hour waiting for tea. Firstly, I couldn't sleep for a moment on this cot all night. And on top of that, I was given a blanket to cover myself with. It wasn't even cold, so I shivered in the cold all night... You all slept comfortably.

Nar... Seeing Dinesh fussing like this, Godavari sits on the thin bed on the floor, shivering from the cold.

Godavari45... angrily... yes, you should also try sleeping on the bed below one day. Hey, you've only been given a blanket to cover yourself. Among those sleeping below, two people get one blanket. Don't start blabbering every morning.

Dinesh50... trembling with anger... huh... Godavari, I beg you, I don't have a good temper with the cold anyway... Now, don't bother me this early in the morning. 

Nqr...Watching the mother-in-law and father-in-law bickering over morning tea, the five daughters-in-law were sitting in the open kitchen in the courtyard, where, due to the extreme cold today, there was a heavy fog and a cool breeze.

Madhavi 25...Shivering. Huh huh huh. This time, the cold weather in December is very bad. It used to be this cold only in January. And yet, we haven't made any preparations for the cold. We haven't bought any warm blankets, clothes, or anything.


Champa 24... (Normal) Huhuhu Madhavi Bhabhi, we'll think about preparing for the cold later. Right now, I have to make tea for Papa Ji, and the firewood is all gone. How will we light the stove without wood? If we had gone to the forest yesterday and collected firewood, we wouldn't be having so much trouble making tea and water.

Babita 22... (Normal) You're right, younger sister-in-law. In this cold weather, we can't manage without tea. For now, we'll have to figure out some way to light the stove.

Narrator... All five daughters-in-law start thinking of a way to light the stove, but there wasn't a single piece of wood available for fuel. Just then, Nupur sees the sack of chaff kept next to the stove.

Nupur 19... (Happily) Oh, I completely forgot that we have dry chaff! We can use that to light the fire and make tea.

Kusum 21... (Normal) Well, then what are we waiting for, sister-in-law? Quickly take the chaff out of the sack.

Narrator... As Nupur touched the sack of chaff, she found it cold and damp from being soaked in dew all night, and all the chaff inside was wet.

title: Delhi Dil Se LIVE : सस्ते दामों में फैशन का खजाना | Janpath Market In Delhi | Connaught Place Tour
description:
#janpathmarket #delhistreetshopping #connaughtplace #delhivlog #zeednh 

Delhi Dil Se LIVE : सस्ते दामों में फैशन का खजाना | Janpath Market In Delhi | Connaught Place Tour

जनपथ की मुख्य सड़क पर कदम रखते ही आपको स्वागत करता है एक अथाह समुद्र – दुकानों का, स्टॉल्स का, और लोगों का... बाईं ओर फैले हैं रंग-बिरंगे कपड़ों के ढेर, दाईं ओर चमचमाती एक्सेसरीज... सुबह के 10 बजे से ही यहाँ भीड़ लग जाती है, टूरिस्ट्स से लेकर लोकल्स तक.. सड़क के किनारे बने स्ट्रीट फूड वेंडर्स मोमोज, चाट और कॉर्न भूनते नजर आते हैं, जो भूखे शॉपर्स को लुभाते हैं... आगे बढ़ें तो छोटी-छोटी गलियाँ मिलती हैं, जहां हैंडलूम स्कार्फ्स और जूतों की दुकानें सजी हैं। कीमतें? बस 200-500 रुपये से शुरू! सौदेबाजी यहां का राजा है – थोड़ी मुस्कान, थोड़ी चतुराई, और आपका सामान 30% सस्ता। पर्यावरण के लिहाज से भी यह मार्केट कमाल का है, रिसाइकल्ड फैब्रिक्स से बने कपड़े मिलते हैं। लेकिन सावधान, चोरी-छिपे पॉकेटमारों से! हमारी सैर जारी रखते हुए, देखिए कैसे यह बाजार दिन-रात एक रंग बदलता है – रात में लाइट्स चमकती हैं, और पार्टी वाइब्स हवा में घुल जाती हैं। यहाँ की हवा में दिल्ली की मस्ती बसी है, जहां हर कोई हंसता-खिलखिलाता शॉपिंग करता है। चाहे आप सोलो घूमें या दोस्तों के साथ, यह वॉक आपको थका नहीं, बल्कि तरोताजा कर देगा। आगे की यात्रा में हम फैशन आइटम्स पर डाइव करेंगे, लेकिन अभी तो बस महसूस कीजिए इस बाजार की पल्स। जानपथ सिर्फ खरीदारी का स्थान नहीं, बल्कि एक लाइफस्टाइल है जो आपको अपनी गिरफ्त में ले लेता है। तो चलते रहिए, अगला स्टॉप इंतजार कर रहा है।

Stepping onto Janpath's main road, you're greeted by a vast ocean – of shops, stalls, and people... To your left, piles of colorful clothes, to your right, glittering accessories... The crowds start gathering as early as 10 am, from tourists to locals... Street food vendors line the road, grilling momos, chaat, and corn, enticing hungry shoppers... Further on, you'll find narrow lanes lined with shops selling handloom scarves and shoes. Prices? Starting from just 200-500 rupees! Bargaining is king here – a little smile, a little wit, and you can get your goods 30% cheaper. This market is also amazing from an environmental perspective, offering clothes made from recycled fabrics. But beware of pickpockets! As we continue our stroll, watch how this market transforms from day to night – the lights twinkle, and party vibes fill the air. The spirit of Delhi is palpable here, where everyone is laughing and enjoying their shopping. Whether you're exploring solo or with friends, this walk won't tire you out, but rather invigorate you. On our next leg of the journey, we'll dive into the fashion items, but for now, just feel the pulse of this market. Janpath isn't just a shopping destination, it's a lifestyle that captivates you. So keep walking, the next stop awaits.

---

👉 **What is Aloo Bedmi?**  
Aloo Bedmi is a traditional **North Indian breakfast**, especially popular in Uttar Pradesh and Delhi, made with a spicy potato curry served alongside deep-fried  puris (Bedmi Poori). But this recipe is special — it follows the **Aligarh-style**, where the flavors are bolder, spicier, and full of local touch.

💬 In this video, we’ll show you:
✅ How to make  Bedmi dough  
✅ Tips to get crispy and puffed pooris  
✅ Perfect blend of spices for the aloo sabzi  
✅ A complete plate that’s perfect for festivals, weekends, or special occasions

📌 **Why You Should Try This Recipe:**
– Authentic Aligarh street food taste  
– No fancy ingredients – simple and easy to follow  
– Great for weekend breakfast or brunch  
– Loved by all age groups – kids to elders  
– 100% vegetarian and made with pantry staples

---

title: Delhi Election 2025: 20 रुपये की कंबल और 30 रुपए की खाट, दिल्ली में कैसे कटती है मजदूरों की रात?
description:
The capital city, Delhi, transforms into a major tourist destination during winter. People love the cold weather, but this comfort is only for those who have a home to stay in, food to eat, and warm clothes to wear. For the city's poor and homeless, however, these winter nights turn into a nightmare.
In this report, witness how the working-class struggles to get through the cold nights. Some rent a cot for ₹50 per night, while others have no choice but to sleep on the streets. Some seek shelter in night shelters, but due to poor conditions and hooliganism, they are often forced to return to the footpaths.
Watch this exclusive report by Shubham Vishwakarma from Khabargaon to uncover the harsh reality of Delhi’s cold nights…

----------------------------

देश की राजधानी दिल्ली सर्दियों के मौसम में एक खास पर्यटन स्थल बन जाती है। यहाँ की ठंडी जलवायु लोगों को बहुत पसंद आती है। लेकिन यह आनंद सिर्फ उन्हीं के लिए होता है जिनके पास रहने के लिए घर, खाने के लिए भोजन और पहनने के लिए गरम कपड़े होते हैं। वहीं, यही सर्दी दिल्ली के गरीब और बेघर लोगों के लिए एक डरावनी रात में बदल जाती है। हमारी इस रिपोर्ट में देखिए कि मजदूर वर्ग के लोग किस तरह अपनी रातें बिताने को मजबूर होते हैं। कुछ लोग हर रात 50 रुपये देकर खाट किराए पर लेते हैं, जबकि कुछ सड़क किनारे सोने के अलावा कोई दूसरा विकल्प नहीं पाते। कुछ लोग रैन बसेरों में शरण लेते हैं, लेकिन वहां की बदहाल स्थिति और गुंडागर्दी से परेशान होकर फिर से फुटपाथ पर लौटने को मजबूर हो जाते हैं।

खबरगांव के इस वीडियो में शुभम विश्वकर्मा की रिपोर्ट में देखिए दिल्ली की ठंडी रातों की काली सच्चाई...

title: जयपुर की इस Bedai Kachori और आलू की सब्जी को लड़कियां खाने से भी घबराती है | Jaipur Street Food
description:
जयपुर की इस Bedai Kachori और आलू की सब्जी को लड़कियां खाने से भी घबराती है | Jaipur Street Food


Jaipur Street Food, Jaipur Food, Indian Street Food, Street Food India, Jaipur Street Food Latest Video, Authentic Rajasthani Food In Jaipur, best street food in rajasthan, street food in jaipur at night

Follow for more content @BeautifulGulabiNagri 

In the narrow lanes of Jaipur’s old city, there is a small shop that has become a legend among food lovers – Radhika Chat Bhandar. This place is known far and wide for one thing: their fiery Bedai Kachori, also called Bedmi Poori.

What makes it special is not just the crispiness of the kachori, but the way it is served – with a piping hot, extremely spicy aloo ki sabzi that will set your taste buds on fire. People from across Jaipur, and even from outside the city, come here just to experience this unforgettable combination.

It’s more than just street food; it’s a taste of Jaipur’s old-world charm, wrapped in spice and tradition.

जयपुर के पुराने शहर की तंग गलियों में एक छोटा-सा ठेला है जिसने खाने के शौकीनों के दिलों में खास जगह बना ली है – राधिका चाट भंडार। इस जगह की पहचान है इसकी तीखी और ज़ायकेदार बेदई कचौरी, जिसे कई लोग बेदमी पूरी भी कहते हैं।

इसकी खासियत सिर्फ कुरकुरी कचौरी नहीं है, बल्कि इसके साथ परोसी जाने वाली गरमा-गरम और बेहद तीखी आलू की सब्ज़ी है, जो हर बाइट को यादगार बना देती है।

यही वजह है कि लोग जयपुर के कोने-कोने से, और बाहर से भी, सिर्फ इस स्वाद का मज़ा लेने यहां आते हैं। यह सिर्फ स्ट्रीट फूड नहीं, बल्कि पुराने जयपुर के स्वाद और परंपरा की झलक है।

Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah is a comedy show inspired by the famous humorous column 'Duniya Ne Undha Chashmah' written by the eminent Gujarati writer Mr. Tarak Mehta. This show revolves around the Gada Family which consists of uneducated businessmen Jethalal Champaklal Gada, Jethalal’s Wife Daya & their naughty Son Tipendra Gada living in Gokuldham Co-operative Society' and covers topical issues which are socially relevant. In case of a problem and emergency, Jethalal Gada often rushes to Taarak Mehta to seek his help and guidance as he finds a philosopher in him. description:
#nahari #olddelhi #streetfood 

Purani Dilli — jahan har subah masalon ki khushboo aur nahari ka swaad milke bana dete hain asli Dilli ka nashta! 🍲
Aaj hum laaye hain Purani Dilli ki 5 mashhoor nahari walon ki kahaniyaan —
jisme har dukaan ka apna rang, apni pehchaan aur apna swaad hai ❤️

👇 Ye rahi Purani Dilli ki top 5 legendary Nahari:

1️⃣ Kallu Nahari – Purani Dilli ka naam lo aur Kallu bhai ki nahari na yaad aaye, aisa ho hi nahi sakta!
Ghee mein doobi, masalon se bhari aur swaad mein lajawab – ye hai Dilli walon ka favourite spot.
(9654794412)

2️⃣ Imran Mustafa Nahari (35 Years Old) – Keval 35 saal purani, lekin taste mein pure nawabi level!
Imran bhai ki nahari ka swaad itna narm aur rich hai ke har niwala dil jeet leta hai.
(7291043309)

3️⃣ Shabarati Nahari (Since 1957) – 1957 se chali aa rahi, ye dukaan Dilli ki purani tehzeeb ka hissa hai.
Yahan ka zayka simple nahi, ek legacy hai – purani recipe, wahi purana swaad!
(9582035786)

4️⃣ Noora Nahari (Barah Hindu Rao – 70 Saal Purani) – Dilli ke purane logon ke liye Noora sirf dukaan nahi, ek yaad hai.
70 saal se zyada purani ye jagah har subah ek hi cheez ke liye mashhoor hai – asli Delhi wali nahari!
(9953522481)

5️⃣ Haji Shidu Nahari (100 Saal Purani) – Ye to Dilli ki asli virasat hai!
100 saal purani is dukaan ki nahari ka swaad time ke saath aur behtareen hota gaya —
har niwala purane Dilli ke jazbaat aur mohabbat se bhara hota hai ❤️
(8920389445)
⸻

description:
#tastefulsafar

Hello Friends,

Welcome to the Tasteful Safar: Journey with Taste and Trust.

Bhogal Chole Bhature Wala is a renowned eatery in New Delhi, celebrated for its delectable chole bhature—a classic North Indian dish that combines spicy chickpea curry (chole) with deep-fried leavened bread (bhature). Established in 1962, this establishment has been serving patrons for over six decades. 

Location and Timings:

Situated at 3/84, K G Marg, opposite Scindia House in the Janpath area of Connaught Place, Bhogal Chole Bhature Wala operates from 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM.  The nearest metro station is Rajiv Chowk, accessible via the Yellow and Blue Lines. 
https://g.co/kgs/o5JpYPo

Menu Highlights:

While their signature chole bhature is the main attraction, the eatery also offers other popular dishes such as chole chawal (chickpeas with rice), matar kulcha (spiced peas with leavened bread), and paratha (a type of flatbread).  The bhature are known for being fluffy with multiple layers, and the chole is uniquely prepared, often including kofta (fried dumplings) and masala aloo (spiced potatoes). 
Given its popularity, the eatery often experiences crowds, especially during peak hours. It's advisable to plan your visit accordingly to ensure a pleasant dining experience.

title: Jama Masjid Market, Matia Mahal, and Chitli Qabar are some of the hubs for Eid shopping and eating
description:
Matia Mahal and Jama Masjid Market During Ramadan

Matia Mahal and Jama Masjid Market in Old Delhi become vibrant and bustling hubs during Ramadan. As the holy month progresses, these areas come alive with festive energy, attracting thousands of visitors for shopping and dining.

Shopping Scene
Matia Mahal, a famous street near Jama Masjid, is known for its traditional markets filled with stalls selling clothes, bangles, attar (perfumes), skullcaps, prayer mats, and decorative lights. The market remains open late into the night as people shop for Eid celebrations.
    Food Delights
The area is equally famous for its mouth-watering iftar (evening meal to break the fast) and sehri (pre-dawn meal) options. Food stalls and restaurants offer kebabs, biryanis, nihari, sheermal, shahi tukda, and refreshing drinks like rooh afza. Karim’s, Al Jawahar, Aslam Chicken and other eateries serve traditional Mughlai delicacies that draw huge crowds.

We travelled from Da Nang to Huê by road, one can also travel to Huê in Train. We had sent one of our team members to Huê on a train so that we can also get clips of the train journey that we will upload in Harish Bali Travels. We did not opted for train journey as we wanted to see Hai van pass. 

Then we proceeded to Huê Airport to board the flight for Hanoi. The activities which we did in between the day, Huê Airport, Hanoi dinner you will be seeing in the BTS episode.

After this we ended the day. Hope you enjoyed the video.

Pahar Ganj ke Naam mein PAHAR hai, Par yahaan asliyat mein koi PAHAR nahi hai 🙂

So for today, I cover 5 Places you should visit in Pahar Ganj for its Food. Kuch aapke suggestions ho to comment mein likh dijiye jee 🙂

Janta Sweets

Normal jagah hai par aapko milenge aise samose jiske andar maa ki dhuli daal ki stuffing hai.  Uske saath  Subzi, Seasonal mooli ke lacche, aur ghiye ka achaar.

8102, Gali No.8, Multani Dhanda, Paharganj, New Delhi, Delhi 110055

Chawla ke Chur Chur Naan
Aapne Butter Naan Khaynege honge, Stuffed Naan khaye honge, par Chawla ke Chur Chur Naan agar nahi khaaye then kisi din Khane chahiye jee. Take any 2 Types ki Gravy (Karri, Dal Makhni, Shahi Paneer, Chole etc.) with Raita, Salad & these Chur Chur naans will make you Khush.

8955, Multani Dhanda,
Open from 12 pm – 4 pm & 7 pm – 11 pm
098719 81988

Radhe Shyam Subhash Kumar Bhature Chole
Amongst Delhi’s Top 3 Chole Bhature, Radhey Shyam serves Chole Bhature from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily. Bas humesha Bheerr lagi rehti hai.

098111 03164

Banke Bihari Samose Gulab Jamun
They are mashoor for their Kachori Subji, Samose Subji and the World Famous Gulab Jamun. Kaafi Purana Naam hai inka and jab bhi jaao bheerr lagi rehti hai.

title: BEST Pocket Friendly Breakfast Spots in Connaught Place
description:
Most Asked Question

Tikku jee, Connaught Place mein kya khaaye, Accha bhi, pocket Friendly bhi

So jee, we have made many reels on this par. Long, detailed video ki demands thi, so here it is.

Now, if you're wondering WHY CP, then the answer is bahut offices hai yahaan and Rajiv Chowk is a Junction of Many metro Lines and because it is the centre of the city hai so, people find CP to be the best meeting point 🙂

These places are Pocket-friendly. Do not expect Gourmet Food here, but it Does the Job Well. 

Aapne Reel to dekh li hogi, let me also share the names and addresses again for more straightforward Navigation.


Poha Corner—This is a Small street-side shop open from 9 to 2 (until Stocks Last). It Sells Poha, Corn Chaat, and Namkeen Daliya at Pocket-friendly Prices. It's a regular place for people working around for a quick, healthy breakfast.
Behind Mc.Donalds, ECE House. Connaught Place



Baba ka Dhaba -  is a 40-year-old Shop where many Ministers and Celebrities have eaten. It is a Frequent Breakfast, Lunch, and Mid-Meal spot for people working in the Ministry or the Government office nearby and for Tourists and Food Lovers like me. Do try their Thalis, Samosa Chole, and gulab jamun.

10 am to 9 pm
Stall No 2 &3, Jantar Mantar Road, Janpath, Connaught Place, New Delhi, Delhi 110001

Kutty’s
Just next to Baba Ka Dhaba, This Shop dishes out Dosas every minute it's Open. Dosa ki variety bhi hai, Vada bhi Milega, idli bhi 🙂

Janpath, Connaught Place, New Delhi, Delhi
9:30 am to 9:pm (Sunday Closes at 6 pm)
 098738 69738



Dhaba Food

Again, a 40-year-old shop. Dhaba Food Serves, Chole Bhature, Rajma Chawal, Kadhi Chawal etc.

Dikhne mein acche, Khaane mein acche 🙂

Shop No. 129, Municipal Market, Super Bazar Compound,
Near Shankar Market, Connaught Place, New Delhi, Delhi 110001
Hours: 9am to  6 pm
Phone: 099715 59206



Odeon Sweets

Yeh dukaan bhi mein bachpan se ja rha hu. Inke Gulab jamun bhi acche, Inke Gol gappe bhi, Inke Chloe Bhature bhi acche aur inki Mithaiyan bhi 🙂

22, Shaheed Bhagat Singh Marg, 
Gole Market, New Delhi,110001
8:30 am to 9:30 pm
Phone: 092106 40716

title: I tried every dish in Food Mall | Mumbai Pune Expressway | Food Challenge | #Bha2Pa
description:
#foodcourt #mumbaipuneexpressway 

During our road trip along the Mumbai–Pune Expressway, we stopped at the Khaugalli Food Mall to take on the fun challenge of eating for just ₹200! With so many food stalls offering tasty dishes, we had to choose carefully to enjoy the best food without spending too much. We started at Kailash Sarovar, where we enjoyed a classic Ghee Dosa and Sabudana Khichdi, a great South Indian start. Next, we visited Egg Sunday for a delicious Half Fry Up. At ATR, we had nutritious Ghee Podi Millet and Bene Idli. To cool down, Yo Boba served us a refreshing Lemon Iced Tea, perfect for the hot highway weather.

We didn't want to miss Sai Sandwich, where the Chocolate Sandwich and Veggie Cheese Grill gave us a fun street-style snack. Then, we tried Shree Krishna Vada Pav, famous for their Vada Pav and Misal Pav combo, which felt like comfort food. At Good Luck Café, we enjoyed a rich Bun Butter Omelette and a cup of Tea, giving us that classic Irani café feeling on the go. To experience authentic Maharashtrian flavors, we stopped at Aapla Maharashtra for Pithla with Bhakri. For some North Indian street snacks, Kailash Parvat served us spicy Raj Kachori and crispy Panipuri. Finally, our trip ended on a tasty note at South & More, where we had Filter Coffee and Ghee Dosa. Each place was special and full of delicious flavors, making this ₹200 food challenge an exciting and tasty adventure filled with local favorites!

Aligarh Numaish is not just an exhibition; it's also a paradise for food lovers. As you walk through the fair, the delicious smell of kebabs, biryani, and sweets like Nan Qatai and Halwa Paratha fills the air. From Nahari, Korma and Mutton Mandi  to rich desserts, there’s something for everyone. It’s a place where you can enjoy the tasty flavors of Aligarh while exploring the lively stalls and attractions.

Aligarh Numaish is scheduled in the month of February every year and it is a must visit place for food enthusiasts.

You can call it Aligarh Numaish 2025 or Aligarh Exhibition 2025 you can find everything you need in it.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) It's good that we took out all the winter clothes from the bed and trunk today and washed them properly.  The cold weather has just started. Later, when it gets colder, it will be very difficult to wash clothes in cold water.

Neha: (28 years old, normal) You're absolutely right, Didi. The weather is nice today, there's even a little sunshine.  It's true that the cold has started, but it's not too much of a problem yet. When it gets really cold, it will be much more difficult to wash clothes and do other chores involving water.

Narrator: Both of them wash the winter clothes and hang them on the roof to dry. After that, they come down to the courtyard and water their plants and crops.

Payal: (30 years old, worried) Oh, whenever I look at the rest of my garden, seeing the beautiful flowers makes me happy. But as soon as I come near this part, my mind goes completely crazy.

Neha: (28 years old, normal) This is nothing, Didi, this is just the beginning. Just wait and see what happens next.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) You're absolutely right, the whole game is yet to unfold. Let's make lunch, it's almost lunchtime.

Narrator: Both of them go inside the house. They were just going towards the kitchen when their mother-in-law, Shanti, stops them and says:

Shanti: (55 years old, normal) Hey daughters-in-law, make some food, I'm very hungry.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) Yes, Mummy ji, we were just about to make food.

Shanti: (55 years old, normal) Okay, but what are you going to make for food?

Neha: (28 years old, normal) We were thinking of making matar paneer (peas and cottage cheese curry), Mummy ji.

Shanti: (55 years old, normal) Oh, forget matar paneer, what's so special about it? You both do one thing, make a nice potato and cauliflower curry today, it will be delicious!  Payal: (30 years old, normal) But Mom, the cauliflower hasn't even started growing in the courtyard yet. So where will we get cauliflower from? There's still time. The winter is still mild, so we can eat other vegetables for now.

Shanti: (55 years old, normal) Never mind, that's why I told you a long time ago to sow the seeds, but no, both of you are too lazy to work. Now you know, we eat potato and cauliflower curry every winter, nothing else. Do one thing, make some poha for me for now. I'll eat some peanuts too, that will satisfy my hunger, and go to the market and bring back potatoes and cauliflower today itself. Potato and cauliflower curry should start being made at home from today.

Narrator: Hearing this, a look of sadness spreads across Payal and Neha's faces.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) Okay Mom, we're going.

Narrator: The two of them first make poha for Shanti, and Shanti sits comfortably watching TV and enjoying the poha. Meanwhile, Payal and Neha leave for the market with a bag.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) I thought we had a few more days, and until the vegetables grow in the courtyard, we could eat other vegetables, but Mom has ordered us to eat potato and cauliflower from today itself.

Neha: (28 years old, angry) Honestly, Didi, I'm so angry too.  There's a limit to everything, who eats so much potato and cauliflower? Now, potato and cauliflower will be made every day in the winter. Our in-laws are the stingiest people ever. They want to grow cauliflower at home, and cauliflower is cheap, that's why only potato and cauliflower will be made. Huh.  They have so much money, what would happen if they spent a little money on vegetables?

Payal: (30 years old, normal) They measure and weigh everything; they don't let a single rupee go to waste.  We've really ended up in a very stingy family.  Narrator: They both go to the vegetable vendor and buy vegetables.

Payal: (30 years old, normal) Hey brother, please give me 5 kilos of cauliflower and 5 kilos of potatoes.

Vegetable Vendor: (45 years old, normal) Okay, sister.  Should I give you any other vegetables too?

Neha: (28 years old, normal) No, brother, we only cook potatoes and cauliflower in the winter, so just give us these.

Vegetable Vendor: (45 years old, normal) Oh madam, eat other vegetables too! There are so many other delicious vegetables in the world. Why are you stuck on just potatoes and cauliflower?

title: Unseen Shekhawati Wedding Food/प्रीति भोज in Mandawa, Rajasthan I Sweets, Namkeen, Ker Sangri, Bade
description:
Mandawa, a small town in Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan, has become a favourite wedding destination because of its royal touch—ornate havelis, cobbled streets, and a timeless heritage that set the perfect backdrop for celebrations. We were here to witness the chaak bhaat ceremony of Shubham and Tamana, a pre-wedding ritual steeped in warmth, tradition, and flavour.

The day began early with preparations for the preeti bhoj, the community feast that brings everyone together. The kitchen buzzed with activity—khasta kachori being fried to golden perfection, halwa gently bubbling, ker sangri slow-cooked with local spices, and aalu vada and dahi vada being carefully plated. The flavours were bold and spicy, with besan and legumes as key ingredients.

After the rituals, guests were welcomed with flavoured milk and snacks. The main course began, as tradition dictates, with four kinds of sweets and namkeen served first. Only then did the rest of the meal follow, offered with warmth and generosity.

What we witnessed was more than just a meal—it was a deep-rooted food tradition where community, celebration, and flavour come together. A cuisine shaped by the desert, built on humble ingredients, and carried forward with pride and affection.

title: #AD Can I Eat For A Full Day In Delhi with Just ₹750?
description:
Tried eating in Delhi for a full day with just ₹750 and honestly it turned out better than expected.
Started the day at Andhra Bhavan with a proper South Indian breakfast. Filling, comforting and great value for money. After that I went to see India Gate or whatever was visible that day.

Lunch was classic Delhi food. Palak paneer, rice and papad from Jain Chawal Wale. Simple, quick and exactly what you want when you are eating on a budget.

By evening hunger kicked in again while waiting for the match, so instead of stepping out I ordered a snack at home. Tried Cheetos International Cheese which is now available on Blinkit for around ₹100. Cheesy, crunchy and easy to snack on.

Dinner was at Majnu Ka Tila with laphing and a hot bowl of thukpa and I ended the day with a beer gelato. Full day done and challenge sorted.
