About the show :- 
_________________

Crime Patrol is a gripping Indian television series that brings to life real crime stories from across the country through powerful dramatizations and thought-provoking narratives. Each episode reflects how ordinary moments—an uneasy silence, a lingering stare, a heated argument—can spiral into unimaginable tragedies when the warning signs are ignored. The show explores not just the crime itself, but the emotional triggers, behavioral shifts, and overlooked instincts that often precede it, asking: could the crime have been prevented if we had paid closer attention? By highlighting the psychological and social cues behind criminal acts, Crime Patrol urges viewers to stay alert, trust their instincts, and understand that awareness is the first step to safety. Through its realistic storytelling and focus on justice, the series also honors the tireless efforts of law enforcement and the resilience of victims, serving both as a cautionary tale and a tribute to the fight against crime.

title: 120/- Rupay Me Dilli Ka Sabse Aacha khana 🫣🤣😱 #youtubeshorts #streetfood #trending #shorts
Ep - 17, Sarojini Nagar Food Tour l Khandani Pakoda + Kulcha King + Shahi Dahi Bhalle + Amar Jyoti
description:
On a rainy afternoon, we set out to explore Sarojini Nagar, a neighborhood that most people know for its bustling markets and bargain shopping, but few truly pause to experience through its food. What we discovered was a trail of iconic eateries, each with its own history, flavours and stories that have been feeding generations.

Our journey began at the legendary Khandani Pakode Wale, a place that has become synonymous with monsoon cravings. The rain outside made every bite of their pakodas even more comforting - from the crunchy soya stick pakoda to the rare kamal kakdi, along with gobhi, baigan, mirchi, dal and paneer pakodas. All of it came alive with their signature chutney.

We then moved on to Shahi Dahi Bhalle. Soft, melt-in-the-mouth dahi bhalle, topped with curd, chutney and a few dry fruits that gave it its “shahi” name. Every bite was a dance of flavours in the mouth. Hence people get drawn to this irresistible dish. 

At Kulcha King, we met the warm-hearted Avtar Singh, who spoke about how the place began and what keeps it thriving. His crisp tandoor baked kulchas, served hot with chole and a tangy imli chutney, felt like food that comforts both heart and hunger. 

Next came Durga Sweets Corner, where the paneer wale bhature stole the show. Soft, puffed bhature paired with rich chole made it one of those dishes you instantly want to come back for. 

We also sat down with Surjit Singh Arora of Amar Jyoti Restaurant, who shared how he once dreamed of joining the army but instead chose to carry forward the culinary legacy of his family. His food speaks for itself - smoky bhatti paneer tikka, butter-soft garlic naan, and a comforting dal tadka that could easily win anyone over.

As the day wound down, we made our way through the lanes of the Sarojini Nagar Market and stopped at Sai Juice Corner. With a glass of chilled, tangy shikanji in hand, we ended our food walk on a refreshing note, the rain still falling lightly around us.

 This rainy day exploration was a reminder that some of the best food journeys aren’t in fancy places but in the heart of local markets, among people who cook with passion and pride.

title: World SAMOSA Day l Delhi Samosa Trail l Japani, Matar, Moong Dal, Afghani, Mutton, Aloo, BBQ & more
description:
World Samosa Day is celebrated on September 5th, and on its eve, we set out on a dedicated Samosa Trail across Delhi, exploring the many forms, flavours, and philosophies behind this much-loved snack.

Our journey begins in the historic lanes of Chandni Chowk at Manohar Dhaba, home to the legendary Japani Samosa. Unlike the usual triangular form, this samosa stands out for its multi-layered, ultra-flaky pastry, fried to a delicate crisp. Each bite shatters into thin layers, revealing a mildly spiced filling, and is best enjoyed with their robust chole, making it a complete, deeply satisfying plate.

Next, we head to Kinari Bazar, where Sohan Sweets and Radhey Lal Halwai have been serving their matar samosa round the year. These samosas are all about comfort, soft, well-seasoned green peas filling, balanced spices, and a crust that’s crisp yet not heavy. Simple, honest, and immensely flavourful, this is the kind of samosa that keeps patrons coming back across generations.

In Paharganj, Janta Sweets offers a refreshing variation with their moong dal samosa. Lightly spiced and gently aromatic, the filling allows the natural nuttiness of the lentils to shine. What makes it especially interesting is the accompaniment, a warm, mildly spiced sabzi that turns the samosa into a fun snack..

The trail then moves west to Janakpuri, where Samosa Party brings a contemporary twist to tradition. Here, samosas take on playful, experimental avatars, from pizza-inspired fillings to BBQ-flavoured creations. Crisp on the outside and indulgent within, these fusion samosas showcase a mind-boggling variety while still retaining the soul of the classic samosa.

We conclude in Pitampura at the iconic Tilak Munjal, known for their large, generously filled samosas. The samosa is filled with a flavoursome potato filling and is served alongside chole and their signature imli chutney, which adds a sharp, tangy contrast. Hearty and indulgent, this is a samosa that truly eats like a meal.

From old-world halwai to modern-day innovators, this Samosa Trail captures Delhi’s enduring love for the samosa, across generations.

title: Ep 13 East Delhi Veg Breakfast Food Walk l Afeem wale chole + Paper Poori Chole + Amritsari Kulchaa
description:
In today's episode of the Neighborhood Eats series, we take you through the vibrant streets of Krishna Nagar with Rishabh, exploring some of the most beloved breakfast spots that locals swear by. From deep-fried traditional dishes to nourishing juices, each stop had its own charm, flavors, and a touch of nostalgia.

Choudhary Di Hatti, near Lal Quarter Park, was our first stop. The massive queue outside spoke volumes about its popularity. This iconic eatery is known for its crispy, golden-brown pooris paired with a rich and robust chickpea curry. The highlight was a spoonful of curd added on top, which balanced out the bold spices in the chole. The flavors packed a punch, with warm, earthy spices coming through in every bite. Rishabh, a regular here, reminisced about his frequent visits and the comforting taste that keeps bringing him back.

Sajan Juice Centre, also near Lal Quarter Park, was a completely different experience from the usual fried treats. The owner is known for his quirky personality and equally quirky concoction. His signature health juice is a blend of 10-15 natural ingredients and botanicals, mostly bitter and astringent. With its bold, bitter taste, it wasn’t the easiest to drink, but locals swear by its detoxifying properties. Despite its intense flavor, it remains a beloved morning ritual for many in the neighborhood, who believe in its health benefits.

Sharma Bhature Wale in Kanti Nagar was next on our list. If there's one place that defines addictive street food, it's this. Their chole bhature are so popular that they have earned the nickname "Afeem Wale Chole," meaning they’re as addictive as opium. The chole were rich, spicy, and packed with deep, smoky flavors, while the bhature were soft, airy, and perfectly golden. Enjoying this dish on a chilly Sunday morning felt like the ultimate weekend indulgence. Rishabh shared fond memories of savoring this very meal on countless occasions. 

New Delhi Darbar in East Azad Nagar is known for its fried snacks and traditional bedmi poori. As we arrived, the aroma of freshly fried samosas, pakoras, and kachoris filled the air. Rishabh recalled how, whenever guests visited his home, he would rush to this spot to pick up a stash of these deep-fried treats. We decided to try their bedmi poori with sabzi and khasta kachori, which turned out to be a satisfying, spice-laden experience. The crispy texture of the kachori paired with the spiced potato curry made for a classic, hearty breakfast.

Our last stop was Breakfast Point in Chander Nagar, known for its Amritsari Chole Kulche, made the traditional way in a tandoor. The kulcha was multilayered, slightly crisp on the outside, yet soft and fluffy inside, generously topped with chole, imli chutney, and a hint of butter. The highlight, however, was the paneer-stuffed kulcha, which transported Rishabh back to his childhood, reminding him of the ones his grandmother used to make. The combination of smokiness from the tandoor and the tangy chole made this a truly memorable end to our food tour.

This breakfast trail through Krishna Nagar was nothing short of a nostalgic journey through flavors and memories.

title: Ep - 15, Mayur Vihar Ph 1 Street Food Walk l Suji Momo + Chaap hi Chaap + Aunty Vada Pav + Hot chips
description:
In this episode of Delhi Neighbourhood Eats, we arrived at Mayur Vihar Phase 1. Our host is a local—Shipra, a passionate baker who left her job to start her own small bakery business. She took us around her neighborhood to explore some of the everyday food spots that locals love. What followed was a trail filled with comfort food, unexpected finds, and inspiring stories of women vendors carving out their space in the street food scene.
We began our walk with a sugarcane juice stall to beat the heat. Ganne ka raas always gives you a sugar rush and is incredibly refreshing, but it's best enjoyed in moderation. Here, the juice was mixed with mint leaves and lemon, which gave it a zesty twist.
Our next stop was a stall named China Town, a busy van known for its Chinese delicacies. But what really caught our attention was the unexpected presence of rajma chawal on the menu. Curious about how it would taste coming from a Chinese food stall, we gave it a try—and we were pleasantly surprised. The rajma was creamy, spicy, garlicky, and the beans were perfectly soft. A solid, comforting plate of food.
Then we visited Chatka Momo, a stall that lives up to its name. They serve vegetarian momos that are maida-free, made primarily from sooji with a small amount of whole wheat flour. We tried their paneer and soya momos, along with their veg spring rolls. What stood out were the four condiments served with the momos—schezwan sauce, peanut butter, mayonnaise, and mint chutney. The paneer momos were juicy and flavorful, while the soya ones were a bit dry, but overall, it was a satisfying experience.
As we moved further, we came across a South Indian food stall run by Jayalakshmi, a woman from Tamil Nadu. At the time we stopped by, there were no customers. In conversation, she shared how business had been slow, with South Indian snacks not being as popular in this area. Despite the competition, she continued to serve food with warmth and a smile. We tried her paniyaram and dosa, both of which had a comforting, homely taste. To help draw more customers, we suggested she experiment with ingredients like butter and paneer. She is working hard to make ends meet, and vendors like her truly deserve our support.
Next, we visited another woman-led stall called Aunty Ji Ke Mashoor Vada Pav. Originally from Bihar, she started this cart with her son, who learned to make vada pav in Mumbai. The soft buns were generously stuffed with green chutney, ghati masala, and a crisp aalu fritter. The taste was surprisingly close to the Mumbai original—simple, spicy, and satisfying.
We then made a quick stop at South Indian Hot Chips, a snack store that specializes in freshly made chips with distinct South Indian flavors. With branches across the city, they prepare daily fresh batches that are packed and even exported. We sampled kela chips, aalu pudina chips, aalu ginger chips, kathal chips, and aalu lachha chips—each one crisp and full of flavor.
The real indulgence began at Mitra Di Chaap, a local favorite for chaap lovers. The variety here was immense. On the owner's recommendation, we tried their veg keema kaleji, shahi paneer, dal makhani, garlic naan, pyaaz roti, Amritsari chaap, garlic chaap, and soya Punjabi tikka. Each dish was well-spiced, rich, and deeply satisfying—a proper chaap feast to remember.
We ended our trail with a sweet treat from Kremella, where we tried their indulgent Lotus Biscoff and Nutella cheesecakes. Rich, creamy, and impossible to resist, they were the perfect end to our street food journey. Finally, we closed the meal with a refreshing paan.

Best DEOGHAR (City of Dahi) Street Food Tour l Moori Ghugni + Dahi Halwa +Samosa Jhalmudi + भाँग गली
description:
In today’s episode, we take you on a vegetarian street food tour of Deoghar with our host Anurag, who came all the way from Ranchi to guide us through the city’s hidden flavors and local legends. Our journey began at Hari Om Nashta, where the sight of hot pakoras welcomed us. Raja Ji prepared a delightful mix of muri, chura, ghugni, aloo dum, chutneys and more. Along with this, we enjoyed crispy aloo chop and crunchy dal vada, light yet zesty snacks that set the perfect tone for the day.

As we moved towards Tower Chowk, we stumbled upon Mohan, a jhalmuri vendor with a mobile setup on his bike. His counter had compartments filled with fresh ingredients like muri, bhujia, peanuts, chana, chutney and even samosa pieces that he cut with scissors. All these were tossed together into a tin, creating a hearty snack for less than 30 rupees. Interestingly, Mohan doesn’t have a fixed stop, moving around the city to serve his flavorful mix.

Next, Anurag took us to Shri Ram Paratha Shop in Paratha Gali, where we tried the sattu paratha served with tangy achar and mustard chutney. The paratha was crisp and flavorful, perfectly fried in oil. From there, we headed to Sashi Bhushan Rai Road for a glass of kesariya lassi, which unfortunately was a bit disappointing as there was no trace of saffron and the yogurt was slightly sour.

The mood changed at our next stop, Gyaneshwar Ji’s shop near Chandni Chowk, known for its luscious halwa made with sooji, a little maida and ghee. It reminded us of the divine kada prasad served in gurudwara. Here, we discovered a local tradition of pairing sweets with yogurt and tried the halwa with curd. The combination turned out to be unexpectedly delightful.

Right opposite was Namkeen Chaat Bhandar, where a plate of poha caught our eye. What looked like simple poha turned out to be crispy fried chura topped with fried vegetables. We also tasted gandhari saag ke pakode and aloo chop with chura, and they were absolutely delicious.

Our next stop was Shri Ganesh Peda Bhandar, where we tried another unique combination, gajar ka halwa with yogurt. Despite carrots being out of season, this pairing tasted surprisingly good. Then we visited Banarasi Chaat House near Siksha Sabha Chowk, which boasts an A-to-Z menu with 26 varieties of chaat. We opted for the tikki chaat served in a kulhad, and it was hot, flavorful and full of taste.

Before wrapping up, we explored Bhang Gali, where we met Manju Ji and Naval Ji grinding bhang leaves into a paste on a sil-batta in their courtyard. They shared fascinating stories about bhang and its association with Lord Shiva.

Our final stop was Hotel Kamdhenu near Tower Chowk Road, where the owner, Ravi Harnani, told us about the legacy of this iconic place and how it continues to remain a favorite among locals and travelers.

From crispy snacks to unusual sweet and yogurt pairings, hearty chaats and cultural traditions, this street food tour in Deoghar was an unforgettable experience filled with flavours and stories that truly define the culinary canvas of the city.

title: Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga | Gupt Bhimashankar | Bhimashankar Temple Tour Guide | Food | Hotels
description:
Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga Darshana🔱📿🌿✨️

Discover the divine tranquility of Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga, one of the 12 sacred Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva, nestled in the picturesque Sahyadri mountain range of Maharashtra! This ancient shrine, around 110-125 km from Pune, is a blend of spirituality, history, and breathtaking natural beauty.

Bhimashankar is not just a pilgrimage site; it's an immersive experience where lush greenery, dense forests, and the serene Bhima River create a truly mystical atmosphere. The temple's architecture, a mix of old and new Nagara style, showcases intricate carvings and ancient craftsmanship. It's believed that the original Shiva Lingam here is "Swayambhu" (self-manifested).
Beyond the main temple, explore the Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary, home to diverse flora and fauna, including the unique Malabar Giant Squirrel (Shekru). You can also visit nearby attractions like the Ram Temple, Devi Temple, and the mystical Gupt Bhimashankar, believed to be the original source of the Bhima River.

Whether you're seeking spiritual solace, an adventurous trek, or simply a peaceful escape into nature, Bhimashankar offers an unforgettable journey.
Highlights of this video:
 * Reaching Bhimashankar from Pune

title: First Time in Delhi – Street Food Chaos, Kebabs & Delhi Belly 🤯
description:
We’ve landed in Delhi, and this was my first time in India—what an incredible, mind-blowing food experience! We explored Old Delhi’s chaotic streets, from Zakir Nagar to bustling roadside stalls, discovering some of the most iconic Delhi street food I’ve ever tasted. This wasn’t just any food vlog—it was a deep dive into authentic Indian street food, from sizzling galouti kebabs and seekh kebabs cooked right on the roadside to rich, velvety nihari stew served in bustling alleyways.

In Zakir Nagar, we found the best nihari in Delhi—a melt-in-your-mouth beef dish bursting with spices and perfectly slow-cooked meat. Just steps away, we stumbled upon skewers of buff kebabs cooked over open flames and packed with bold masala flavors. The seekh kebabs were spicy, aromatic, and unbelievably juicy—this is the true taste of Old Delhi kebabs and authentic Delhi street food.

Then came the big butter chicken battle. We visited both Moti Mahal—the legendary birthplace of butter chicken—and a rival spot also claiming to have invented this iconic dish. We compared traditional butter chicken with creamy, tomato-rich gravy to a modern version with a lighter, smoother texture. Trust me, the debate over the best butter chicken in Delhi is far from over!

The adventure continued with crispy fried chicken from a hidden street stall, rich goat brain curry from Karim’s, and buttery romali rotis that paired perfectly with the bold Delhi street food flavors. We also savored sizzling tandoori chicken, chapli kebabs packed with mint chutney, and a showstopping inverted butter chicken drenched in sizzling butter.

This trip wasn’t just about food—it was a full-on sensory overload. The sounds of the streets, the heat of the Delhi sun, the thick air filled with spices and smoke, and the sheer energy of the people made this Delhi food tour unforgettable. Whether you’re searching for the best butter chicken, rich nihari, or the boldest seekh kebabs in Delhi, this video captures it all.

🎥 Filmed in Delhi, India, 2025—featuring Zakir Nagar nihari, Karim’s goat brain curry, Moti Mahal butter chicken, and the chaos of Old Delhi street food tours.

title: Baba Baidyanath Dham Darshan & Deoghar Special Maha Prasad PEDA, Jharkhand l Jyotirlinga Temple Ep 1
description:
Just before the sacred month of Sawan began, we travelled to Deoghar in Jharkhand, home to the Baba Baidyanath Dham, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and among the most important Shiva shrines in the country. This visit was made possible in collaboration with Trip to Temple, our travel partner for this journey.

We began the day at the temple. First we met one of the main priests. The queues were already building. After a long wait of nearly four to five hours, we finally made it inside for darshan. The experience was powerful, crowds of pilgrims and an atmosphere soaked in chaos and devotion. He then shared stories about the temple’s mythological origins, its connection to Ravana, and why it holds such deep significance for so many. Though Anubhav had visited before, he felt the place revealed something new each time, especially just ahead of the Sawan rush.

Of course, Deoghar is also known for its peda. After the darshan, we made our way to the famous Peda Wali Gali, a bustling street lined with sweet shops stacked with trays of freshly made peda. We stopped at Kanhai Lal and Sons, a shop with a long-standing legacy. A chat with the owner gave us insight into their process, their history, and what makes their peda stand out in a town full of sweet makers.

We ended the day with some much-needed comfort at Awantika, a place known for its Bengali snacks and sweets. This journey, like many others, weaves together food, culture, and lived experience,

title: Subah 5 Baje Jama Masjid ka Street Food | Chapli Kabab, Lassi aur Kachori Ka Zaika 😋😋
description:
#jamamasjidstreetfood #streetfood #olddelhi 
Don't forget to subscribe

Dilli ki subah kuch khaas hoti hai, lekin Jama Masjid ke aas-paas ki galiyon mein jab khana banta hai, toh hawaon mein bhi zaika ghul jaata hai. Subah ke 5 baje jab puri Dilli soti hai, yahan zindagi chakhne ke liye jag chuki hoti hai.

⸻

Episode 1: Afghani Samosa Restaurant – Subah ki shuruaat Chapli Kabab ke saath

Subah ki pehli roshni ke saath hi Jama Masjid ke ek kone mein se ek khushbudar dhuaan uthta hai — ye hai Afghani Samosa Restaurant. Yahan ke Chapli Kabab ka jadoo aisa hai ke ek bite lete hi lagta hai jaise Peshawar ki galiyon se Dilli aa gaye ho. Garam, masaledar aur halka crispy — ye kabab subah ke sardi mein ek garmahat le aata hai.

Phir aata hai shawarma roll, jismein chicken ka juicy pan se nikalta mazza aur garlic mayo ka creamy touch milke ek dum behtareen street treat banata hai. Aur unka Afghani chicken samosa — bhai sahab, ismein sirf murgh nahi, mohabbat bhara hota hai. Har ek samosa mein Afghani spices ka asli touch milta hai, jo ise aam samose se kahin upar le jaata hai.

⸻

Episode 2: Kamaal Sweets – Mithaas aur Subah ki Shaan

Thoda aage chalte hi milta hai Kamaal Sweets ki shop, jahan se ghee ki khushboo aati hai jo seedha dil tak jaati hai. Yahan ki sabzi puri ek dum ghar ke taste jaisi — halke masale wali aloo ki sabzi, aur garam, phooli puriyan — aise lagta hai jaise maa ne tiffin mein rakhi ho.

Aur halwa-matri ka combo toh kamaal ka hai! Karare matri ke saath jab suji ka garam halwa milta hai, toh lagta hai jaise Dilli ne apna dil tumhare plate mein rakh diya ho. Subah ka nashta agar Kamaal Sweets ke bina karein, toh woh adhoora lagta hai.

⸻

Episode 3: Mamu Bhanje Ki Khasta Kachori – Ek Purani Dilli ka Zaika

Jama Masjid ke ek dusre mohalle mein milta hai Mamu Bhanje ki Kachori. Naam hi kaafi hai — aur unki khasta kachori waise hi kaafi hai! Har kachori ke andar masaledar daal ki filling hoti hai, aur upar se woh itni karari ki aawaz aapke kaanon mein bajti hai. Sath mein milti hai khatti-meethi chutney aur dahi — bas, subah ban jaati hai.

Mamu bhanje ke thele ke aas-paas hamesha bheed hoti hai, lekin har kisi ke chehre pe ek hi cheez hoti hai — tasalli.

⸻

Episode 4: Mohd Yunus Milk Store – 80 Saal Ki Thandak

Nashta jab ho jaaye, toh kuch meetha-thanda ho jaaye. Uske liye perfect jagah hai Mohd Yunus Milk Store, jo lagbhag 80 saal se Jama Masjid ki galiyon mein apna swad banaye hua hai. Yahan ki dahi ki lassi — bhai, kya kehne!

Ghada mein bani thandi, ghadhi hui lassi jo dahi ke asli swad ko barkarar rakhti hai. Upar se malai ki ek moti layer aur thoda pista — har ghoont mein purani Dilli ka zaika, aur nayi Dilli ka pyaar milta hai.

⸻

Ant mein ek baat:

Jama Masjid ke yeh chhote chhote food joints na sirf khana dete hain, yeh yaadein dete hain. Har nashta, har swaad ek kahaani kehta hai — mohalla, parampara aur pyar ki kahaani.

Agar Dilli ko subah mehsoos karna hai, toh ek din 5 baje Jama Masjid ki galiyon mein zaroor aaiyega.

title: Ranthambore Travel Guide 2025 | Jungle Safari, Luxury Stay & Things to Do in 2 Days
description:
Planning a trip to Ranthambore? In this complete Ranthambore travel guide, we share everything you need to know for a 2–3 day road trip from Delhi NCR or Gurgaon to Ranthambore National Park. Thanks to the new Delhi–Mumbai Expressway, you can now reach Ranthambore in just 4 hours from Gurgaon, making it a perfect weekend getaway.

We stayed at the luxurious Aamaghati Wildlife Resort, just minutes from the safari gates, where we experienced a mix of comfort, Rajasthani culture, and wellness with the Sri Sri Spa. In this vlog, we take you through:

Ranthambore Jungle Safari – spotting tigers, deer, and wildlife in core zones
Things to do in Ranthambore – visiting Ranthambore Fort, Trinetra Ganesh Temple, Dastkar Ranthambore, Ranthambore School of Art, Rajiv Gandhi Museum of Natural History, Kala Gaura Temple & Chauth Mata Temple
Food & Culture – enjoying Rajasthani food, folk dance performances, and shopping local crafts.

This vlog is your complete Ranthambore itinerary – combining adventure, history, spirituality, and luxury stay. Whether you’re visiting for tiger safari or a peaceful family vacation, this video will help you plan the perfect trip.

Best time to visit Ranthambore: October to March (but tiger sightings are amazing in summer too!)

दिल्ली में भारी बारिस के बाद जाम की स्थिति है.. यमुना नदी के बढ़ते जलस्तर को देखते हुए, मजनू का टीला से सलीमगढ़ बाईपास तक आउटर रिंग रोड पर यातायात बुरी तरह प्रभावित है। वज़ीराबाद-सिग्नेचर ब्रिज और चंदगी राम अखाड़ा-आईपी कॉलेज रेड लाइट से यातायात डायवर्जन लागू रहेगा।

कश्मीरी गेट रिंग रोड पर यमुना बाढ़ का पानी आने से ट्रैफिक बहुत धीमी गति से चल रहा है। मजनू का टीला की ओर जाने वाली रोड पर ट्रैफिक की गति बहुत धीमी है, पुलिस भी तैनात है। सिविल लाइन की ओर जाना चाहेंगे तो अंदर के रास्ते को बंद कर दिया है। उस रास्ते पर पानी भर रखा है।

Commuters are advised to avoid these routes, use alternate routes, avoid roadside parking and follow the instructions of traffic personnel for smooth traffic.

Old MANALI Food Tour l Sabali + Lazy Dog + Dylan’s + Corner House + Chopstick + Chha Meat + Kukkad
description:
We went on an Old Manali food tour with our host, Khushboo Barry, an entrepreneur who also runs a homestay in the valley. Manali, with its snow-draped peaks, pine-covered slopes, and the Beas River rushing through, has long been a travelers’ haven. Beyond the views and mountain air, the food scene here is equally fascinating, shaped by locals, long-term settlers, and visitors from around the world who have made it their home.

Our first stop was Sabali Bakery, started by a Sudanese man and his wife. Over the years it has grown into one of the most happening spots in Old Manali, especially popular with the young international crowd. The menu is colorful, eclectic, and full of energy. We tried a refreshing chia pudding, a soft bagel with cream cheese, and a delicate matcha tart, each reflecting the café’s global spirit.

From there we walked to Dylan’s Coffee House, an iconic name in Old Manali. The café has a loyal following of travelers who return again and again for its cozy atmosphere and irresistible bakes. We had the chance to meet one of the founders, who shared their journey of starting the café and nurturing it into the landmark it is today. Their legendary secret cookies lived up to the reputation, and the strong bulletproof coffee gave us just the right kick to carry on with our day.

Next on the trail was The Lazy Dog Café, where we were welcomed by its owner, once a TV journalist, who traded the newsroom for the warmth of hospitality. He shared stories of how the café took shape along the banks of the river. The food here was exceptional—perfectly cooked rainbow trout fish, a fresh smoked chicken salad, and sushi rolls that brought a touch of Japanese finesse to the mountains.

The Cornerhouse Restaurant and Café was our next stop, run by Siddharth, a young entrepreneur and trained chef. His menu reflects both his culinary skills and his love for experimenting with flavors. We sampled the beetroot carpaccio, fried chicken wings, lamb burger, and pan-seared trout fish, each dish crafted with attention to detail. Paired with some Belgian ale, it made for a truly satisfying meal.

To balance all this modern flair, we then visited Chopsticks, one of the oldest and most reliable places in Manali. Known for hearty Tibetan fare, this stop was all about comfort. A steaming bowl of mixed gyathuk, with its broth rich in flavor and noodles perfectly cooked, was just the kind of soulful food one craves in the mountains.

We couldn’t resist a sweet detour at Jeet Sweet Shop, an old-style mithai shop tucked into the town. Walking in felt like stepping back in time, with trays lined with traditional sweets that have been part of Manali’s food culture for generations. We tasted their khoye ki burfi, dal ki burfi, nariyal ki burfi, along with besan ki burfi, crispy namak pare, and sev buniya. Each bite carried the charm of recipes that haven’t changed in decades.

The food tour came to a fitting close at Kachnar Restaurant, where we were served a curated Himachali meal. The spread included chha gosht, a mutton curry cooked in yogurt-based gravy, and Himachali kukkad curry, both paired with hot tandoori rotis. The meal ended on a sweet note with meetha bhat, a fragrant sweet rice dish. 
This journey through Old Manali’s cafés and kitchens was more than just about food, it was about the people, their stories, and the way flavors from around the world have found a home in this mountain town.

description:
PURANI DILLI CHOLE - Weekend ka matlab something special for the whole family. What better than this Old Dilli style Chole Kulche 😋😋

***********************
𝗔𝗠𝗔𝗭🥘𝗡  𝗦𝗛🍳𝗣

🔪Knives I use - https://amzn.to/4kzSJVe

***********************
𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗰𝗸 𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗼𝗼:
Tari wale Chane
Instant Chole - 
***********************

PURANI DILLI CHOLE

Preparation time 15 minutes
Cooking time 25-30 minutes
Serve 2-4 

Ingredients
For Cooking Chole
500 gms Chickpeas (soaked overnight) भीगे हुए छोले
½ tsp Turmeric powder, हल्दी पाउडर
2-3 no. Garlic cloves (optional) लहसुन
Prepared bouquet garni, मसालों की पोटली
Water as required, पानी
3 tbsp Ghee, घी
Salt to taste, नमक स्वादअनुसार
3-4 tbsp Tamarind pulp, इमली का पानी
1 tsp Jaggery, गुड़
4 heaped tbsp Prepared masala, तैयार किया हुआ मसाला
1 tsp Black peppercorns, crushed, कुटी हुई काली मिर्च
½ cup Chickpeas water, छोले का पानी
Prepared tira, तैयार किया हुआ तीरा
2 tbsp fresh Coriander leaves, chopped, धनिया पत्ता

For Bouquet garni
3 no. Black cardamom, बड़ी इलायची
2 tsp Black peppercorns, काली मिर्च के दाने
1 tbsp Tea leaves, चायपत्ती
3-4 no. Cloves, लौंग
4 no. dry Kashmiri red chillies, सूखी कश्मीरी लाल मिर्च

For Masala
3 tbsp Coriander seeds, धनिये के बीज
½ tbsp Cumin seeds, जीरा
3-4 tbsp Black peppercorns, काली मिर्च के दाने
7 no. Black cardamom, बड़ी इलायची
8-10 no. Green cardamom, हरी इलायची
4-5 no. Cloves, लौंग
1 tsp Fennel seeds (optional) सौंफ़
Salt to taste, नमक स्वादअनुसार

For Gajar Mirch Ka Achaar
1 cup Water, पानी
2 medium Carrots (peeled & cut into batons) गाजर
2 no. Green chillies (less spicy & roughly chopped) हरी मिर्च
Salt to taste, नमक स्वादअनुसार
1 heaped tbsp Vinegar, सिरका
2 tbsp Jaggery, गुड़
1 tsp Degi red chili powder, देगी लाल मिर्च पाउडर
¼ tsp Turmeric powder, हल्दी पाउडर
½ tsp Coriander powder, धनिया पाउडर
1 tsp dry Mango powder, आमचूर पाउडर

For Ginger Green Chilli Paste
4 inch Ginger (peeled & chopped) अदरक
5 no. Green chillies (less spicy & roughly chopped) हरी मिर्च

 For Tira
3-4 tbsp Oil, तेल
2-3 tbsp Ghee, घी
1 tsp Cumin seeds, जीरा
Prepared Ginger Green chilli paste, अदरक हरी मिर्च का पेस्ट
A pinch of asafoetida, हींग
2 heaped tbsp Degi red chili powder, देगी लाल मिर्च पाउडर
200 ml Ghee, घी

For Searing Kulcha
1 tsp Ghee, घी
2 no. Kulcha, कुलचा
1 tbsp Prepared tira, तैयार किया हुआ तीरा

Other Ingredients
3-4 tbsp Red tamarind (soaked for 1hr) भीगी हुई लाल इमली

For Garnish
Coriander sprig, धनिया पत्ता
Green chilli, slit into half,  हरी मिर्च
Lemon wedge, नींबू की फांक

Process 
For Cooking Chole
● In a pressure cooker, add soaked chickpeas, turmeric powder, garlic, prepared bouquet garni, water as required, ghee and mix well.
● Cook it for 3-4 whistles until cooked well.
● Open the lid, add salt to taste, tamarind pulp, jaggery, prepared masala, crushed black peppercorns, chickpeas water and let it simmer for 10-12 minutes until thickens.
● Finish it with prepared tira and fresh coriander leaves.
● Transfer it to a serving dish, garnish it with coriander sprig, green chilli and lemon wedge.
● Serve hot with seared kulcha.

For Bouquet Garni
● Take a small piece of muslin cloth, add black cardamom, black peppercorns, tea leaves, cloves, dry kashmiri red chillies and make a potli of it.
● Keep it aside for further use.

For Masala
● In a pan, add coriander seeds, cumin seeds, black peppercorns, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves, fennel seeds, salt to taste and dry roast them until it's aromatic.
● Transfer it to a mixer grinder jar and grind it into fine powder.
● Keep it aside for further use. 

For Gajar Mirch Ka Achar
● In a pan, add water, carrots, green chilli and let boil it for 7-8 minutes.
● Add vinegar, jaggery, degi red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, dry mango powder and simmer for 4-5 minutes.
● Transfer it to a bowl or cleaned jar and keep it aside for further use.

For Ginger Green Chilli Paste
● In a mortar pestle, add ginger, green chillies and grind it into coarse paste.
● Keep it aside for further use.

For Tira
● In a handi, add oil, ghee, once it's hot, add prepared ginger garlic paste, a pinch of asafoetida and cook it for 2-3 minutes.
● Add degi red chili powder and cook for a minute on low flames.
● Finish it with ghee and let it cook for a while.
● Turn off the flames and keep it aside for further use.

For Searing Kulcha
● In a pan, add ghee, once it's hot, place kulchas, pour some prepared tira and sear the kulchas on both the sides until it's golden in colour.
● Transfer it to a serving dish and serve hot with prepared chole.

title: I Tried India’s Most Disgusting Street Food
description:
Kolkata, India 

I went to Kolkata, India, to try one of the most infamous street food stalls in the country — the Club Kachori street vendor Lali Chhangani. This tiny roadside shop has become famous (and controversial) because people online call it India’s most disgusting street food. From the dirty setup to the way the food is served, this vendor has gone viral for all the wrong reasons.

But here’s the thing… Club Kachori is also one of the most famous breakfast foods in Kolkata. Locals still line up for a plate of puris with spicy potato curry every morning. I had to experience it myself to see if it really is as unhygienic as everyone says.

In this video you’ll see my full reaction to eating the famous Club Kachori in Kolkata, the reality of the stall, and why it has such a shocking reputation.

title: Special Peshawari Siri Paye Recipe | Peshawari Head and Legs Making Process -Paye Nashta Street Food
description:
Discover the authentic Special Peshawari Siri Paye Recipe, a traditional breakfast delicacy from the heart of Peshawar, Pakistan. Watch the full head and legs making process as skilled street food chefs prepare this rich and flavorful Paye Nashta using age-old techniques and spices. This Peshawari street food is famous for its deep aroma, slow-cooked broth, and melt-in-the-mouth texture, served hot with naan. Whether you call it siri paye, paye, or trotters curry, this is one of the most iconic Pakistani street foods loved by locals and tourists alike. Perfect for food lovers, culinary explorers, and desi food fans around the world. Join us in the streets of Peshawar and experience the magic of traditional cooking. title: Best Himachali Dhaba Food in Manali |Kangana Ranaut’s Mountain Story, Siddu, Alfajor, Lugdi, Thentuk
description:
This Manali food tour is all about slowing down, eating local, and discovering stories behind popular eateries. Hosted by Khusboo Barry, the journey focuses largely on dhabas and some new places that reflect the everyday food culture of the region.

We began at Bread of Life, a South American bakery started by Juan Carlos, who hails from Chile, along with his wife from Bolivia. They found their home in Manali and built this warm little bakery rooted in memories and comfort. From empanadas with tartar sauce to alfajors born out of nostalgia, the food here carries personal stories and a beautiful cross-continental connection.

Our next stop was Fat Plate Manali, where we met Anubhav and his mother, the force behind Rati’s Homemade Preserves, jams, and pickles. Her journey is truly inspiring. From being an ex-principal to becoming an entrepreneur. She lovingly walked us through how it all started, the local fruits she works with, and the best ways to enjoy her products. Simple, honest, and full of warmth, just like her preserves.

We then headed to Kalzang Dhaba, a cosy, home-style setup offering comfort food with a view. This is the kind of place where you feel instantly welcome. We tried rice beer, veg momo, siddu, rajma chawal, fiddlehead fern sabzi, and shakkar ghee roti. The food was divine and the mountain views simply unforgettable.

While trekking nearby, we met local shepherds from the Gaddi tribe. Sitting and talking with them gave us insight into their food habits, lifestyle, and the struggles they face in the mountains. Our next destination was The Village Café, where we enjoyed pasta and thenthuk. The owner shared stories about the café, its beginnings, and their journey in Manali, making the meal even more memorable.

We wrapped up the tour at The Mountain Story, a restaurant by Bollywood actress Kangana Ranaut. Here, we tried the Pahadi non-vegetarian thali featuring local delicacies. The food was satisfying, and the ambience reflected a strong regional identity.

This episode is a mix of dhabas, restaurants, heartfelt stories, and local encounters that gives a glimpse into Manali beyond the usual tourist lens.

The Best Breakfasts in Delhi? Let’s Settle This! 😳🔥
description:
Delhi does breakfast like nobody else, and this episode proves it. As part of 28 Weeks 28 States, I’m exploring India one morning meal at a time — and today’s stop took me straight into the heart of the capital for two absolute legends.

The day began in the lanes near Jama Masjid, where a hot, slow-cooked nihari with a soft khamiri roti reminded me exactly why Old Delhi is unmatched. Deep flavours, tender meat, and that perfect hit of chilli and ginger — it felt like Delhi giving me a warm morning hug.

From there, I rode to Paharganj for a plate that every Delhiite swears by: chole bhature from a decades-old institution. Airy bhature, rich chole, and flavours that hit all the right notes. If this is how Delhi does breakfast, I can’t wait to see what the next state brings.

title: Delhi’s Veg Food Is On Another Level! 🍽️💚
description:
Delhi continues to surprise with how good pure vegetarian food can be. I spent the day exploring two iconic spots that prove you don’t need meat for a mind blowing meal. From old school flavours in the busy lanes of Purani Dilli to a freshly rebuilt favourite in Pandara Road, this one turned into a proper comfort food tour.

The first stop set the tone with a layered kulhad bowl brimming with pulao, chole, palak and all the little touches that make Delhi street food special. Then I headed to a beautifully restored restaurant to try a thali loaded with classics. The freshness of the sabzis, the richness of the dal and the soft paneer all reminded me why this city’s vegetarian scene has such a loyal fanbase.

If you love simple ingredients coming together in surprising ways, this Delhi chapter is going to make you hungry. Come experience the flavours of the capital with me.

title: Ep 12 East Delhi Non Vegetarian Street Food Walk l Kharode + Cream Chicken, Ch Soup + Keema Mutton
description:
As a part of our Delhi Neighbourhood Eats series, we embarked on a flavourful journey through Geeta Colony, East Delhi guided by our host, Gagan Ji, who introduced us to some legendary food joints in this bustling hub of non-veg delicacies.  

Our first stop was Tilak Kharode Wale, a name synonymous with mutton delicacies for years. From brain to tongue, trotters, and mutton keema, their menu is a treasure trove for meat lovers. We tried the trotters followed by tongue, discovering the rich flavors that make these dishes a local favourite.  

Next, we visited Patiala Shahi Food Corner, renowned for their hearty soups. Their chicken soup stood out with its thick, peppery, and buttery flavour. Its taste was elevated by a secret spice mix that adds a unique touch.  

Chawla's Chick Fish was our third destination, a haven for fried and tandoori delights. Their fried chicken and fish are crowd-pullers, with patrons enjoying their meals parked in their cars. We tried their fish tikka, made from fresh surmai fish, which was perfectly soft and meaty.  

At Kamal Meat House, another legendary joint, we indulged in chilli chicken and keema mutton. The chilli chicken was a delightful twist on the classic, featuring fried chicken tossed in butter with capsicum, onions, and three types of gravies. The keema mutton, on the other hand, was packed with robust spices and tender meat, a true treat for meat enthusiasts.  

Sachdeva Chicken Corner was next, where we sampled creamy chicken and butter chicken on Gagan’s recommendation. The creamy chicken lived up to its name, featuring a rich curry of cream, milk, and mild spices. The butter chicken, while flavorful had a pronounced tomato base that added a tangy punch.  

To conclude our walk, we visited Kalra Sweets for a sweet finale. Their gajar ka halwa and gulab jamun were freshly made, offering the perfect balance of sweetness and richness to end the evening on a high note.  

This food walk with our friend Gagan was a fascinating gustatory journey through the diverse and delicious offerings of Geeta Colony.

description:
✨🚗 The adventure rolls on! Our dream journey – the Bangalore to Ladakh Road Trip 2025 in our trusted Maruti Suzuki Baleno – continues.
In this second episode, we cruise from Nagpur to Agra, crossing vibrant states, endless highways, and soaking in the essence of the open road 🌄🍴. Along the way, we share unfiltered road trip stories, food stops, stay options, and real highway vibes that make the journey unforgettable.

#BangaloreToLadakh #LadakhRoadTrip2025 #BalenoRoadTrip #MarutiBaleno #IndiaRoadTrip #NagpurToAgra #NH44RoadTrip #TravelVlogIndia #ExploreWithCar 🚙✨

In this video, we share:
✅ Complete route details of Nagpur to Agra by car
✅ Road conditions on NH44 across Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
✅ Food stops & overnight stay options during the drive
✅ Tolls, fuel, and cost breakdown for Day 2
✅ Drone shots, scenic drives, and our real unfiltered conversations on the highway

This is not just a cinematic travel vlog, but also a practical road trip guide for anyone planning a Bangalore to Ladakh journey by car.

🚙 About the Bangalore to Ladakh Road Trip 2025

Starting Point: Bangalore, Karnataka
Ending Point: Leh–Ladakh, Jammu & Kashmir
Distance: ~3,200 km (one-way)
Vehicle: Maruti Suzuki Baleno (Yes, we are doing Ladakh in a hatchback 🚗💪)

This vlog series will cover each day in detail:
Bangalore → Nagpur → Sagar (MP) → Agra → Jammu → Srinagar → Kargil → Leh → Nubra Valley (Diskit–Hunder–Turtuk) → Pangong Tso → Hanle → Tso Moriri → Puga → Pang → Manali → back to Bangalore.

🛣️ Day 2 Route – Nagpur to Agra

Route Taken: Nagpur → Seoni → Lalitpur → Jhansi → Gwalior → Agra
Distance Covered: ~900 km
Driving Time: ~15–16 hours (depending on breaks and traffic)
Highways: NH44 all the way → seamless connectivity
Road Condition: Mostly excellent 4-lane roads, occasional diversions and rough patches near Seoni and Jhansi; smoother stretches closer to Agra.

🍴 Food & Stay Options (Nagpur → Agra)

Plenty of dhabas and small eateries along NH44
Good highway restaurants near Seoni, Jhansi, and Gwalior
Agra offers a wide range of stay options — from budget hotels to premium stays near the Taj Mahal

title: 55 Saal Purani Legacy 🔥 Bilal Chicken Khureji — Buff Boti & Bheja Fry Ka Asli Dilli Taste!
description:
Bilal Chicken — Khureji, Delhi | 55 Saal Purani Legacy 🍗🔥

Dilli ke Khureji ilake ka mashhoor naam — Bilal Chicken!
Yahan ka taste sirf khana nahi, ek virasat hai jo 55 saal se chalti aa rahi hai.
Baap-dada ka diya hua hunar, aur aaj ke time ke perfect flavors — dono ka zabardast combination milta hai yahan.
Is jagah ko chalate hain do bhai — Shamshuddin aur Bilal, jinhone apne mehnat aur taste se har food lover ka dil jeet liya hai ❤️

⸻

🍽️ Specialty Dishes:

🔥 Buff ke Ghost ki Boti – Ye Bilal Chicken ki sabse khaas dish hai!
Soft, juicy aur masalon se bhari boti jo sirf yahin milti hai. Har bite mein ek dum rich aur spicy flavour.

🧠 Bheja Fry – Jo log asli Delhi taste samajhte hain, unke liye yeh dish ek treat hai.
Bilkul creamy texture ke sath masaledar fry — melt-in-mouth experience!

🥩 Seekh Kabab – Tandoor se nikalte hi aroma hi sab kuch keh deta hai.
Perfectly grilled, juicy aur smoky taste — ek baar kha liya to yaad reh jayega.

🍢 Boneless Malai Tikka – Soft, creamy aur thoda mild spice ke sath — family ke liye perfect dish.
Har bite mein malai aur masale ka balanced blend.

🍛 Chicken Changezi – Purani Delhi ka flavour, thick gravy aur tender chicken pieces ke sath.
Ek aisa taste jo roti ya naan dono ke sath kamaal lagta hai.

🧈 Butter Chicken – Creamy, buttery aur thoda sweet-spicy touch ke sath — sabka favourite.
Rich texture aur ekdum smooth gravy.

🌶️ Chicken Chatkara – Naam hi kaafi hai!
Tangy, spicy aur full of flavour — bilkul street-style Delhi wala chatkara.

title: Reality of Indian Street Food
description:
Checkout BeatO CurV here:
Amazon: https://tinyurl.com/YT-Mohak-AMz
BeatO website: https://tinyurl.com/YT-Mohak-Shopify
Flipkart: https://tinyurl.com/YT-Mohak-FK

****** 
India's street food is going viral. But, not for the right reasons. We see videos racking up millions of views that show Indian food as dirty, unhygienic, and absolutely unsafe to consume. Even the latest news reports speak of the same sad state of Indian street food. For instance, just last year in May, a 19-year-old died after he consumed Shawarma in Mumbai that gave him severe food poisoning. A few months back, 97 kids fell sick after consuming Pani Puri in Madhya Pradesh. This is the state of India's street food that we all love to eat. But is this really true? Is India's street food so unhygienic? To find the answers to these questions, I decided to play Hunger Games with my team members. We went to three different cities - Bengaluru, Delhi, and Kolkata to taste and test three of the most famous street foods - Shawarmas, Momos, and Puchkas. And what we found out surprised us.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
The show is inspired from the famous humorous column 'Duniya Ne Undha Chasma' written by the eminent Gujarati writer Mr. Tarak Mehta. This story evolves around happenings in "Gokuldham Co-operative Society" and covers topical issues that are socially relevant. The show predominantly - revolves around 'Jethalaal' (Dilip Joshi) who is an uneducated Gujarati businessman. Your 'Taarak Mehta' (Sailesh Lodha), is his neighbor. 'Jethalaal' finds a friend and philosopher in 'Taarak Mehta' and often goes to him for advice whenever he is in trouble. Jethalaal's family includes his simpleton wife 'Daya Ben' (Disha Wakani) and a mischievous son 'Tapu' (Bhavya Gandhi). Tapu is a menace and a constant source of trouble to all the members of Gokuldham. They have often warned 'Jethalaal' to reform 'Tapu' or else be prepared to leave the premises. Lost hopes of being heard by his son push Jethalaal' to call his father 'Champaklal' (Amit Bhatt) from the village. This was his great idea of leashing some control over the mischievous Tapu. The opposite happens and the grandfather joins hands with the grandson to make life a roller coaster troublesome ride for Jethalaal.

description:
Delhi to Manali road trip | Manali Weather Update 
"Good morning, friends! Welcome back to the channel. Today, we’re kicking off an epic road trip from the heart of India — Delhi — all the way to the beautiful mountains of Manali."

[Footage of hitting the highway]

"With around 540 kilometers to cover, the journey promises changing landscapes, bustling dhabas, winding mountain roads, and unforgettable views. Let’s hit the road!"

[Scene: Driving through Delhi outskirts – sunrise shots]

Voiceover:

"We started early in the morning to avoid the city traffic. As we left Delhi behind, the roads opened up and the first rays of the sun lit up our path. The air slowly started getting cooler as we drove ahead."

[Scene: Driving through Murthal – dhaba stop]

Voiceover:

"Our first pit stop was Murthal — a paradise for food lovers. We grabbed a delicious breakfast of stuffed parathas and hot tea at one of the famous dhabas here. Perfect fuel for the journey ahead."

[Scene: Driving on NH-44, entering Punjab and then Himachal]

Voiceover:

"The drive on NH-44 was smooth, with green fields stretching on both sides. We crossed Karnal, Kurukshetra, and then Ambala. Once we hit Chandigarh, the real fun began — the plains gave way to hills as we entered Himachal Pradesh."

[Scene: Mountain roads, tunnels, Beas River along the road]

Voiceover:

"As we climbed higher, the roads became winding and scenic. The Beas River accompanied us, flowing gracefully alongside. Each turn brought a new view — pine forests, charming villages, and cool mountain breeze."

[Scene: Reaching Kullu Valley – local culture, apple orchards]

Voiceover:

"A quick tea break in Kullu gave us a taste of local Himachali hospitality. The air here was fresh and crisp. From here, Manali was just a couple of hours away."

[Final Scene: Entering Manali – mountain peaks, market views, evening lights]

Voiceover:

"And finally, after a full day of beautiful roads, great food, and unforgettable views, we reached Manali! Surrounded by snow-capped peaks and tall deodar trees, this town feels like a postcard."

[Outro]

Voiceover:

"So that was our Delhi to Manali road trip — full of adventure, nature, and memories. If you’re planning a trip, this is one of the most scenic drives you’ll ever take. Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe if you enjoyed the ride. See you in the next one!"

Govardhan, Mathura Food Tour I ब्रजभूमि का असली स्वाद I Aloo Kachori, Rabri, Khurchan, Sev Paratha
description:
Holi in Govardhan is a time of colors, devotion, and delicious food. The streets are filled with the aroma of freshly fried snacks and traditional sweets. We set out on a street food tour to experience the best local flavors before the festival.  

Our first stop was Harilal Kachori Wale. We had aalu kachori with chutney, a quick and satisfying breakfast. The kachoris were freshly fried in mustard oil, making them crisp and flavorful.  

Next, we visited Shree Nath Ji Misthan Bhandar. If you love rabri, this place is a must-visit. Fresh batches were being made at regular intervals. We were lucky to taste some straight from the kadai. It was thick, creamy, and delicious.  

Chirag Namkeen Bhandar was our next stop. We tried some of their best-selling namkeen, including mota mixture, hing mixture, dal biji, sev, and saloni. Each had a unique taste and crunch.  

At Shree Giriraj Misthan Bhandar, we had bedai kachori with sabzi and chutney. The kachoris were stuffed with moong dal and fried in ghee. The pumpkin sabzi was much loved for its mild sweetness, making the meal even more special. Everything here, from the bedai to the sweets, was prepared in ghee, adding to the rich flavors.  

Shree Govardhan Misthan Bhandar had a variety of sweet and savory snacks. Their aalu tikki chaat was the highlight. The tikki was super crisp, topped with matra, dahi, and chutneys. Every bite was packed with flavor.  

We stopped at Gopal Ji Kanji Vada Stall for a bowl of refreshing kanji vada. The vadas were soaked in tangy mustard-flavored kanji, making it a light yet flavorful dish.  

In the evening, we returned to Shree Giriraj Misthan Bhandar for their samosas. These were one of Anubhav’s favorites. The crisp casing and zesty fried potato filling made them a perfect evening snack.  

Chauni Chacha Parathe Wale was next. Parathas are a filling option, and we tried their sev paratha. Sev, a crunchy namkeen, was mixed with a potato filling and stuffed into the paratha. It was unique and delicious.  

At Shree Giriraj Jalpan Grih, we stopped for a cup of chai. This place is one of our favorites for tea. They also serve coffee and lassi, making it a great spot to relax.  

We wrapped up our food tour at Lala Paan Bhandar. A flavorful paan was the perfect way to end our journey through the festive streets of Govardhan.

title: MASSIVE Lucknowi Muslim WEDDING Dawat FOOD I Fish & Raan Musallam + Lagan Ka Murgh + Mutton Pulao
description:
Weddings in Lucknow are not just about uniting two people but about celebrating tradition, culture, and of course, food. This time, we had the privilege of attending the Dawate Walima celebrations of two newlywed couples—Yasub & Sakina and Nida & Amber. These grand feasts, deeply rooted in Awadhi heritage, bring families and friends together over an elaborate spread of meticulously prepared dishes.

What made these feasts even more special was that the head chefs at both weddings were two brothers—Mohd. Arik and Arshi—culinary maestros who belong to a family that has been perfecting the art of Awadhi wedding feasts for six generations. Their reputation precedes them, with families who take pride in hosting grand meals placing their trust in their expertise. Through their craft, they have kept alive the rich culinary heritage of the region.

We visited both venues to witness the massive preparations taking place behind the scenes. Lucknowites are known for their deep appreciation of good food, so everything had to be executed with precision. Arik and Arshi took charge of the entire process, supervising every step, from marination to the final presentation. As they worked, they explained the intricate details of an Awadhi dawat, and we followed them through the making of some of the most iconic dishes—shahi tukda, sheermal, raan musallam, fish musallam, galouti kebab, and mutton pulao. Watching these dishes come to life firsthand was a true revelation of the expertise, passion and relentless hard work that goes into creating an unforgettable feast.

As evening set in, guests started arriving, and we began our culinary journey at Yasub and Sakina’s wedding venue. There, we had the privilege of tasting raan musallam, fish musallam, and galouti kebab right at the cooking area, in the company of the chefs. Later, we joined the guests to enjoy a delicious spread of rich qorma paired with soft, fragrant naan. Every dish was a testament to slow cooking, perfected over time, and brimming with complex flavors.

Next, we made our way to Nida and Amber’s wedding feast. The spread was equally magnificent, starting with galouti kebabs, chicken tikka, and chicken reshmi kebabs. For the main course, we indulged in rogan josh, lagan ka murgh, and the ever-fragrant mutton pulao. The feast ended on a sweet note with decadent shahi tukda and refreshing kulfi—each bite a delightful blend of tradition and indulgence.

Beyond the remarkable food, what stood out was the warmth and generosity of the hosts. And as we relished each dish, we realized that in Lucknow, feeding people is not just a custom—it’s a cherished tradition, upheld with pride and passion.

title: Ultimate Puri Food Tour | Dalma, Dahi Bara Aloo Dum, Khaja & More | Veggie Paaji
description:
Veggie Paaji is taking you on the ultimate food tour of Puri - The Land of Jagannath 🙏 Get ready for a non-stop flavour festival as we uncover the absolute best vegetarian street food and traditional sweets this sacred city has to offer. We're on a mission to find the "Asli Swaad" (The Real Taste), and trust us, we found it!

Join our ultimate food challenge as we dive into:

➡️ Dahi Bara Aloo Dum: Our first stop in Puri was for this legendary street food! We found an amazing vendor serving incredibly soft lentil fritters (bara) topped with spicy potato curry (aloo dum) and a flavourful pea curry (ghugni). One bite and we were in heaven! 🤤

➡️ Authentic Odia Thali: This is the definition of a true vegetarian feast! With over 10 items like Dalma, Saaga Bhaja, Aloo Chokha, and a rich Mushroom Curry, this thali offers an authentic taste of Odisha in every single bite. So filling, yet our hearts wanted more! 😍

➡️ Spicy Beachside Jhal Muri: You can't visit Golden Beach without trying this! A fiery, tangy, and crunchy puffed rice snack that is an absolute explosion of flavour. Seriously amazing! 🔥

➡️ Famous Khaja Prasad: Near the Jagannath temple, we tried the famous sweet prasad, Khaja. This crispy, flaky pastry soaked in sugar syrup is divinely delicious and simply melts in your mouth.

➡️ Puri's Unique Papodi: This is a dessert you've never seen before! Made from delicate layers of milk cream (malai) and thickened sweet milk (rabri), this sweet left us speechless. We have to come back just for this!

That was our non-stop food tour of Puri! What was your favourite dish? Let us know in the comments below!

title: Ep 4 - Journey to Sailana & Ratlam, Famous Kachori, Bafla, Ratlami Sev exploration & more.
description:
Journey started with view of Mahi river along with tropic of Cancer, We proceeded towards Sailana and saw the famous cactus garden there and then finally ended up spending full day at Ratlam until evening.

Just in case if you have not explored our website you may check out the below link and see the spices that we buy from place of origin and make these available for you in smaller packaging.

Spices website link - https://spice2nuts.com/

Gadgets we use for Visa2explore & Harish Bali Travels.
Sony A 7 111 camera: https://amzn.to/4clE2zI
Z -90 Sony: https://amzn.to/3SO8T10
Go pro Hero 12: https://amzn.to/46GULw6
IPhone 15 Pro: https://amzn.to/3YJgr8Y

For Background Music, we use “Epidemic Sound” in our videos. You can use it from the link below.

https://www.epidemicsound.com/referral/ujnsd6

Date of Journey - 12th September 2025

Maharana Pratap Setu - Built on Mahi River, this bridge plays the role of connecting Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh. Mahi river here is the only river in India to cross the Tropic of Cancer twice.

In case you haven't watched Episode 2 Places to visit in Banswara, Rajasthan. 
Here is the link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uWSsnDqJc90

Kalyan Kedareshwar Waterfall - This is a seasonal waterfall and also a tourist attraction near Sailana, Madhya Pradesh. It is popular locally for its scenic view. 

Bada Kedareshwar Waterfall - This place is known for its natural waterfall that flows over the Kedareshwar Cave Temple in Sailana, Madhya Pradesh.

Sailana Palace - This is a historical palace established in the 18th century and now also home to the erstwhile royal family of Sailana. There is a huge Cactus garden too while having a collection of various cactus plant species. There is a Palace Museum too.
Ticket:  Rs 20 per person

Sailana to Ratlam is about 20 km.

Karu Mama Kachoriwale - This is one of the famous kachori shops in Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh.
Dahi Kachori: Rs 35

Gordhanlal Secwala - Ratlam is known for its Sev namkeen and this shop is one of the oldest and famous shops of Ratlam
Sev Namkeen: ₹ 280 per kg

Vyas Dal Bati - This place is one of the famous food joints in Ratlam. We had lunch here.
Bafla: Rs 10
Kadhi: Rs 25
Dal: Rs 60

Ratlam Chandni Chowk - This place is one of the busy markets of Ratlam. This market is a hub for local handicrafts, textiles, jewelry, etc, which makes it a popular shopping destination for the tourists too.

Mahalwada Ghantaghar - It is known for its historical significance in Ratlam’s  Heritage and Culture. Bending the building there is Ranjit Vilas Palace which is nowadays used for govt offices.

After this we went to 3 different shops to taste and buy Sev Namkeen near Do Batti Rd, Ratlam.
Trimurti Sweets & Namkeen
Sev Namkeen: ₹ 140 for ½ kg

Balaji Palace
Sev Namkeen: ₹ 140 for ½ kg

Jalaram Sweets
Sev Namkeen: ₹ 140 for ½ kg

Lala Satish Chaat House - This is one of the local food stalls near Do Batti Rd, Ratlam. It is famous for its tasty chaat.

Chowpatty - This place is a hub for foodies to enjoy snacks and street food in the evening.

After this we ended our day, hope you enjoyed the video.

title: 24 Hours Eating Old Delhi’s BEST Street Food | Delhi Food Walks
description:
►SUBSCRIBE for 2 new videos every week: https://
www.youtube.com/user/TheMrtaster
►Uzbekistan Food Tour- Iconic Upside Down Uzbeki Bread in Samarkand: https://youtu.be/JJNu_3X3L3A

Join me and my good friend Delhi Food Walks as we explore the vibrant streets of Old Delhi, tasting some of the most iconic and flavorful street foods India has to offer! From sizzling kebabs to royal desserts, this tour is packed with culture, tradition, and unforgettable flavors.

🫓 What I Tried:
 • Khasta Kachori & Aloo Sabzi – Crispy lentil-filled snack with spicy potato curry, masala, and green chili.
 • Golden Indian Tea – Made with milk, tea, sugar, spices, almonds, and saffron.
 • 150-Year-Old Paratha Shop – Parathas with chutneys like pumpkin, aloo mutter, sweet mango powder sauce, and Rabri-filled sweet paratha.
 • Bedmi Poori, Chole Bhature & Samosa with Jalebi – Puffy breads with chickpeas, chutneys, and desserts like Halwa, Jalebi, and Gulab Jamun.
 • Rabri Falooda – A chilled dessert with milk, cardamom, sugar, nuts, and ice.
 • Paan – Traditional betel leaf mouth freshener with colorful fillings.
 • Qureshi Kababs at Jama Masjid – Juicy grilled koobideh, chicken, and beef kebabs, sizzling on charcoal, topped with butter.
 • Chicken Lollipop at Rafiq Chicken Corner – Spicy fried chicken with unmatched flavor.
 • Haji Mohd Hussain’s Fried Chicken – Street-style fried chicken with onion, lemon, and masala.
 • Buffalo Biryani at Mohd Taufiq – Rich and flavorful biryani served hot in Jama Masjid.
 • Shahi Tukda at Cool Point – Traditional dessert with ghee-soaked bread, mango & vanilla ice cream, saffron, almonds, and silver foil.

🎥 This food journey was one of my favorite experiences in India – full of colors, spices, and warmth. Don’t miss this one!

title: Momos🥟#food #foodie #foodvlog #minivlog #india #streetfood #delhi #momos #tasty #comparison #new
description:
This is day 1 of me trying out the various categories of different food items available in the market, ranging from the cheapest to the most expensive versions of those food items. In this video I’ll be trying out the various versions of one of the most popular street food in Delhi, Momos. Momos are arguably the most loved street food in Delhi and is can be found at the corner of almost every street in this city. Various categories of momos are available in Delhi, the most popular one being the cheapest variety which is readily available and is generally priced very reasonably. Other varieties of momos include but are not limited to tandoori momos, Kurkure momos and the expensive high quality steamed dimsums. Surprisingly, all these food items were extremely flavourful and unique in their own way. I had a great time trying out these food items. Hope you guys enjoy the video !

title: Laxmi Nagar Overview Delhi | Local Shopping Market Tour
description:
Delhi का Laxmi Nagar Market, East Delhi का एक प्रसिद्ध और व्यस्त Local Shopping Market है। यहाँ रेडीमेड कपड़े, जींस, शर्ट, टी-शर्ट, जूते, चप्पल, बैग, मोबाइल एक्सेसरीज़, कॉस्मेटिक्स, फैशन आइटम और रोजमर्रा की जरूरतों का सामान मिलता है। बाजार में छोटी-बड़ी दुकानें, शोरूम और स्ट्रीट शॉपिंग के कई विकल्प मौजूद हैं। Laxmi Nagar अपने Coaching Centres और Students की वजह से भी काफी प्रसिद्ध है, जहाँ देश के अलग-अलग हिस्सों से विद्यार्थी पढ़ाई और प्रतियोगी परीक्षाओं की तैयारी के लिए आते हैं। यहाँ Street Food, खाने-पीने की दुकानें और स्थानीय बाजार की रौनक भी देखने को मिलती है। मंगलवार को लगने वाला Mangal Bazaar भी इस इलाके की खास पहचान है। Laxmi Nagar Metro Station (Blue Line) से यहाँ आसानी से पहुँचा जा सकता है। आसपास Shakarpur, Preet Vihar, Nirman Vihar और Vikas Marg के इलाके स्थित हैं। East Delhi के इस व्यस्त बाजार की Shopping, Local Lifestyle और बाजार की रौनक का पूरा नजारा देखिए Bharat Tour के साथ।

title: Hidden Food Gems in Narela Delhi Street Food | Saini Kachori , Gupta Sweets & More | Veggie Paaji
description:
Join Veggie Paaji on an exclusive food tour of Narela, a part of Delhi whose culinary treasures are yet to be discovered online! In this Breakfast Edition, we uncover legendary street food spots that have been serving locals for decades. From a 50-year-old Kachori shop to mouth-watering Chole Bhature and traditional sweets, Narela is a paradise for food lovers.
In this episode, we visit:
Saini Kachori Bhandar: Famous for their delicious Kachori and Puri Sabzi, serving since 1970.

description:
Bihar के Hajipur में गंगा किनारे बसे Chisti गांव और आसपास के इलाकों में बीते 7-8 दिनों से बाढ़ का पानी भरा है। सैकड़ों घर डूब गए हैं, लोग अपने परिवार और बकरियां, गाय-भैंस जैसे जानवरों के साथ सड़क किनारे रहने को मजबूर हैं। बरसात और धूप में बिना छत के रहना, खाने के लिए सातुआ पर गुज़ारा करना, कई लोगों को तीन-चार दिन से पका भोजन नसीब नहीं हुआ। इस दौरान स्थानीय लोगों से बिहार की वर्तमान स्थिति, शराबबंदी, नीतीश कुमार की नीतियों और चुनाव आयोग के SIR (Special Summary Revision) को लेकर भी बातचीत हुई। उनका कहना है कि बाढ़ की यह समस्या लगभग हर साल आती है, लेकिन राहत और समाधान अब भी दूर है। सरकार और राजनीति से अलग, यहां ज़िंदगी बस पानी और इंतज़ार में फंसी है।

title: Rs 99 Street Food Delhi  This Place Sells BEST Ambersari Chur Chur Naan White Butter | Chole Bhature
description:
Rs 99 Street Food Delhi  This Place Sells BEST Ambersari Chur Chur Naan White Butter | Chole Bhature

This place is hands down representing Delhi's Nashta which is their special 35 years old Amritsari Chur Chur Naan, Chole Bhature with their variety of Lassi. The place is called Sanjay Chur Chur Naan in Dwarka Sector 10. The place is known for their Thali starting from Rs. 99. They are totally inspired by Amritsari Culture. They begun at Moolchand in 1990 and people loved their food. The Nashta they present is fresh and buttery. I was drooling while shooting for this place. They have 14 types of Variety of stuffing. The laccha was crispy and flakky. I liked how people were gathered and enjoyed their meals. The place is best enjoyed when having food their at the restaurant. I took permission to record and showcase Delhi's authentic Nashta. Delhi breakfast comes in many forms but Chole Bhature and chur chur naan stands out everytime. You may either choose white butter or yellow butter on top of your parantha. Check out my reaction to this lovely place.

title: Trying Gurgaon’s Most INSANE Street Food | The Urban Guide
description:
Girisha and Neeraj headed out to explore Gurgaon’s most insane street food, and the city completely surprised them with its incredible flavours and vibrant street culture.
Their first stop was the viral Kulcha Wala, known for serving soft, buttery kulchas paired with rich, flavourful chole that has taken social media by storm. Next, they tried Civil Lines wale Chole Bhature — famously known as Virat Kohli’s favourite —, and it absolutely lived up to the hype with its light, fluffy bhature and perfectly spiced chole.
The food trail continued with wheat momos, a healthier twist on Delhi-NCR’s beloved snack, stuffed generously and steamed to perfection. They then enjoyed some authentic Lucknowi kebabs, beautifully cooked with melt-in-the-mouth texture and aromatic spices.
To wrap up the experience, they sipped on refreshing coffee and ended the day with Golgappe, packed with tangy, spicy flavours that left them wanting more.

Let us know in the comments if we missed any iconic spots, and tell us what we should try in Part 2 of Gurgaon’s insane street food tour!

title: Jama Masjid delhi street food Tour Part 1 | Hilal Hotel, Babu bhai kebab, Aslam butter chicken!
description:
I travelled all the way from Pune to the heart of India's capital to spend 48 hours immersing myself in the rich history and even richer flavors of Old Delhi, right next to the iconic Jama Masjid.

Joined by my friend Lali (@LondonkiLali ) we explored the narrow lanes that are famous not only for their chaotic beauty but also for centuries-old food secrets. We ate breakfast, lunch, and dinner at the most iconic spots, and even found some hidden gems that completely blew us away!

🍽️ Our 24-Hours Food Journey Highlights:
 • The Royal Breakfast: We started at Hilal Hotel for the iconic Nalli Nihari, a slow-cooked dish that melted in the mouth and tasted like it came straight from the Mughal courts.
 • The Unexpected Kebab: We found Babu Bhai Kebab Wale and were shocked by how silky smooth and delicious the Chicken Kebab was—it’s simple, subtle, and an absolute must-try.
 • The Vegetarian Surprise: We stepped into Shyam Sweets for a sweet and savory experience: the Bedmi Puri and Sabzi (plus a secret addition of halwa!) that tasted just like Bhandara food, proving Old Delhi has something for everyone!
 • The Controversial Butter Chicken: We tried Aslam's, famous for literally bathing the chicken in butter, and then hunted down the late-night worker-favorite, Ya Allah Chala De Hotel, for a surprisingly delicious white-gravy butter chicken.
 • The Drink of Love: A stop for the universally loved, refreshing Mohabbat Ka Sharbat was essential

title: Furniture DIY from a सब्ज़ी वाला Thela 😳 #shorts #homedecor #craft
description:
Furniture DIY from a सब्ज़ी वाला Thela 😳 #shorts #homedecor #craft

Waise toh i loveee experimenting in my DIYs but ye wala thodaaaa tricky tha 🤪

Here are all the details for this Thela Storage Desk -

➡️ Sabse pehle I replaced the big wheels with smaller ones so that you get enough space btw top and bottom rim jaha aap storage de sako. 

➡️ Now generally these carts don’t have a finished look so I had to cover the top portion with a 20 mm MDF board (directly used nails to fix them).

➡️ For storage, I made cubicles with a thin plywood aur dono ko attach kiya with screws (one in front and one at the back) I knew I was gonna have bamboo baskets in them so i’d say ki aap baskets ke measurements se 0.5-1 inch extra space rakhna. 

➡️ Next everything had to painted WHITE 🖌️ So pehle iron structure pe red oxide primer lagaya and then painted everything (including the plywood) with PU Enamel Paints. 

➡️ Once dried properly (about 24-36 hrs later) table top pe wooden wallpaper lagaya and for that real rustic feel I chose a wallpaper with grooving textures. 

➡️ Lastly made few alphabets for labelling using resin & silicon mould and bamboo baskets pe laga ke storage cubicles me slide in kar diye. That’s how our thela turned storage desk was ready 🥳

Kaisa laga ye transformation, jaldi jaldi batao comments mein 👇🏻

title: EP07 Delhi to Jim Corbett by Car | Road Trip to Kotabagh, Uttarakhand
description:
Embark on an unforgettable Delhi to Jim Corbett road trip by car with us! 🚗🌲 We kicked off our journey from Le Meridien Gurgaon at 11 AM after a hearty breakfast. Covering about 290 KM, our route was Gurgaon-Delhi-Noida-Hapur-Gajraula-Brajghat-Moradabad-Tanda-Bazpur-Kaladhungi-Kotabagh, a scenic path leading to a peaceful destination near Jim Corbett National Park.

Our first stop was a COCO BP pump in Green Park, Delhi, to fuel up. We then cruised through Noida via the Barapullah flyover and gained speed, but hit a 3-hour traffic jam near Garh Mukteshwar. After finally getting back on track, we stopped at Bikanervala around 4 PM for a quick but satisfying meal of Chole Bhature and Lassi.

As we reached Moradabad, we left the main highway that heads to Lucknow and drove towards Nainital via Tanda and Bazpur. Navigating through the dark, we finally arrived at Kotabagh, nestled near Kaladhungi and Jim Corbett National Park.

Join us as we capture the entire experience of driving from Delhi to Jim Corbett by car, exploring the scenic highways, and enjoying delicious food along the way! 🚙

🔑 Keywords: Delhi to Jim Corbett by car, Delhi to Kotabagh by car, Jim Corbett road trip, road trip from Delhi to Jim Corbett, Gurgaon to Jim Corbett by car, driving to Jim Corbett from Delhi, Delhi to Uttarakhand road trip.

title: Secret caste burns bodies to survive (no woman allowed 😲)
description:
I traveled to Varanasi to meet the Dom caste - people who have been burning India's dead bodies for over 3,000 years. What I saw was unbelievable:

- They live right next to burning funeral pyres - over 100 bodies are cremated DAILY
- The same wood they use to burn bodies is also used to cook their food
- Their homes are filled with the smell of burning human flesh
- Many develop serious breathing problems from inhaling smoke their whole lives
- They celebrate a Masaan Holi using ashes from cremations

Despite river Ganga making them sick, these same people are working hard to save it from pollution.

According to local stories, Lord Shiva cursed their ancestors 6,000 years ago, and now they're stuck in this job for generations.

This video isn't just about death rituals - it's about real people living extraordinary lives that most of us can't imagine. You'll see families trying to maintain normal lives while surrounded by death every day. Despite everything, they keep their traditions alive.

Tell me in the comments which part of this video surprises you the most.

title: Best Old Delhi Sehri Night Food Walk | Champa Bread + Butter Jam Sheermal + Khajla, Pheni, Jalebi
description:
We began our sehri food walk in the historic lanes of Old Delhi, covering parts of Ballimaran, Daryaganj, and the areas around Jama Masjid. These neighbourhoods, steeped in centuries of tradition, come alive in a unique way during Ramzan, especially in the quiet, anticipatory hours before dawn.

Next, we stopped by Khan Omelette Corner. Their Khan Special Omelette was a buttery, cheesy affair, rich in calories but undeniably delicious. This indulgent dish is quite the local favourite, especially for those looking to fuel up before a long day of fasting.

Our next stop was Islam Bhai’s night food stall, a humble but vital eatery that runs late into the night. It caters mostly to workers and labourers, offering hearty meals at pocket-friendly prices. The setup was simple, but the energy and sense of community were palpable.

We then made our way to Shamsi Milk Shop, where we had a glass of hot milk. Thick, slightly sweet, and served in a no-nonsense way, it offered warmth and comfort amidst the night’s quiet chill.

Although we didn’t eat at Mohd. Sagheer Nahari Wale, we were struck by the sizeable crowd gathered outside. The popularity of their nihari spoke volumes, and while we didn’t try it, its reputation clearly draws people in even at such early hours.

At Al Haj Bakery, we met the genial owner who walked us through their offerings and the bakery’s history. It was a nostalgic place, where we tried rusk and a few other baked treats. The sense of pride and tradition infused every word he shared.

Flora Bakery was another delightful discovery. The owner introduced us to a wide range of fresh breads and sheermal, all traditionally consumed during sehri. But the highlight was their champa milk bread — soft, fragrant, and rich with stories that added layers of meaning to every bite.

Ameer Sweet House showcased some of their special Ramzan-time delights. We saw and sampled items like meetha samosa, paneer jalebi, khajla, and feni. The display was a feast for the senses, and the variety of textures and flavours reflected the festive spirit of the season.

At Mohd. Shakeel Milk Shop, we ordered a bowl of milk and had it the local way — with champa bread dipped in, accompanied by khajla, feni, and feeki jalebi. The place was buzzing with energy and locals enjoying their early morning ritual.

We ended our walk at Wazeeruddin Tea Stall, where we had a warm cup of coffee. This old establishment carries the charm of a bygone era, and its patrons seem to return not just for the brew, but for a sense of familiarity and comfort. 

As we wrapped up the tour, we came across a sehri wale — a man who walks through the lanes, calling out the names of residents to wake them up for sehri. It was a touching reminder of an old tradition that still thrives in pockets of the city, rooted in community bonds and a deep sense of care.

Haryanvi rapper Dhanda Nyoliwala delivers a compelling performance, weaving relatable narratives with his signature cadence. He's joined by Xvir Grewal, whose melodic interpretation adds another layer of depth to the exploration of love and loss. The production is a vibrant fusion of modern sounds and traditional Haryanvi instrumentation, featuring the distinctive textures of the Deru, Bugchu and Ghada, creating a sonic landscape that is both familiar and refreshingly new
