title: Delhi To Lucknow by Road | Yamuna Expressway | Agra Lucknow Expressway | Full Info | Travel Logs |
description:
Delhi To Lucknow by Road | Yamuna Expressway | Agra Lucknow Expressway | Full Info | Travel Logs |

Delhi to Lucknow by Road: A Journey Across North India
The road journey from Delhi to Lucknow is a fascinating experience that offers a unique opportunity to explore the heart of North India. Spanning a distance of around 550-600 kilometers (depending on the route), the drive typically takes anywhere between 10 to 12 hours, making it a long but enriching trip. The road itself is an essential part of India's vast transportation network, connecting the national capital to the capital of Uttar Pradesh. Along the way, travelers pass through diverse landscapes, bustling towns, and historical sites that showcase India's rich culture and heritage.

Route Options for the Journey
There is primary route for this road trip

Via Yamuna Expressway and Agra-Lucknow Expressway: Another alternative is taking the Yamuna Expressway from Delhi, which leads to Agra. From Agra, drivers can proceed via the Agra-Lucknow Expressway, a state-of-the-art highway that connects Agra to Lucknow. This route, though slightly longer, provides a faster and more comfortable driving experience, especially with less congestion and a well-maintained highway.

Preparing for the Trip
Before setting out, it's essential to prepare adequately for the long road trip. Check your vehicle's condition—ensure that it is well-maintained, has enough fuel, and is stocked with essential supplies like water, snacks, and first aid kits. Since it’s a long journey, it’s advisable to take regular breaks to rest, stretch, and recharge. Also, familiarize yourself with key landmarks, rest areas, and refueling stations along the route to make the trip as smooth as possible.

Highlights of the Journey
The drive from Delhi to Lucknow offers a glimpse into the heart of India. Here are some of the key highlights you can expect along the way:

Delhi to Ghaziabad: As you leave Delhi, the first major city you’ll encounter is Ghaziabad. Located just across the border from Delhi, this bustling city marks the start of your journey through Uttar Pradesh. Ghaziabad is known for its industrial areas, and while it's a busy city, it offers good infrastructure and ample food and fuel options for travelers. This stretch is relatively smooth, and you'll soon find yourself on the NH44 heading toward Meerut.

Meerut and Muzaffarnagar: As you drive further on NH44, you'll pass through Meerut, a historic city that is a hub for education and commerce. Meerut is known for its role in the First War of Indian Independence in 1857. After Meerut, the road continues toward Muzaffarnagar, a district that offers rural views and small towns. The scenery here begins to shift from the urban hustle of Delhi to the quieter and more peaceful outskirts of Uttar Pradesh.

The Yamuna River and Etawah: Continuing on, you will reach the area near the Yamuna River. As you cross bridges over this historic river, you might catch glimpses of rural life along the banks. Further along, you'll approach Etawah, a city of significant historical importance. It is also known for its proximity to the Chambal River, famous for the Chambal ravines. This area has a unique charm with its mix of rural life and modern development.

Agra and the Agra-Lucknow Expressway: If you choose the Yamuna Expressway route, you’ll encounter the city of Agra, home to one of the Seven Wonders of the World—the Taj Mahal. Agra is a great place to stop for a brief break, where you can visit the Taj, the Agra Fort, or just explore the bustling markets. After Agra, the Agra-Lucknow Expressway beckons. This expressway is one of the most modern and well-maintained roads in India, making it a smooth and fast route toward Lucknow.

Fatehpur Sikri: Whether you're on NH44 or the Agra-Lucknow Expressway, you’ll pass near Fatehpur Sikri, another UNESCO World Heritage site. Fatehpur Sikri is a historical city that was once the capital of the Mughal Empire under Emperor Akbar. It’s a site full of historical significance and provides an excellent chance to take a detour and explore Mughal architecture.

Rural Landscape and Small Towns: As you approach the outskirts of Lucknow, the landscape gradually becomes more rural. Small towns, lush fields, and agricultural landscapes come into view, showcasing the beauty of the Indian countryside. The journey’s final leg offers a transition from the bustling urban areas of Delhi and Agra to the more serene atmosphere of Lucknow, known for its old-world charm and modern development.

Arrival in Lucknow
Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh, is a city known for its rich cultural heritage, Mughal architecture, and Nawabi cuisine. Upon arrival, you'll be welcomed by an elegant blend of history and modernity. The city is famous for its vibrant markets, exquisite historical monuments, and delicious food, including kebabs, biryanis, and the famous Lucknawi chikan work.

title: Hunting For Kolkata's Tastiest Street Food 🇮🇳
description:
📍 Every place I've eaten, saved on a map. Five free in every country: https://somewheregood.io?s=yt-desc

In this video, I take you on a DIY food tour through the bustling streets of Kolkata. My adventure begins in the New Market area, where I immediately spot a crowd gathered around a popular sugarcane juice stall. For just 20 rupees, I grab a glass—and it’s one of the best sugarcane juices I’ve ever tasted.

Next, I stumble upon a vendor selling masala chai for only 5 rupees. I can’t resist, so I grab a glass and savor it right on the street. Continuing my walk, I find another vendor serving freshly squeezed orange juice for 50 rupees. It’s as refreshing as it is delicious.

With my thirst quenched, I cross the street in search of food and find a man cooking up fresh dosas. For just 35 rupees, I enjoy a crispy masala dosa while chatting with some locals.

Next, I hop into a classic yellow Kolkata taxi and head to KC Das for a famous rasgulla—a syrupy, cheese-filled dumpling that’s a must-try in the city. Afterward, I wander down a small alleyway and discover a shop selling kathi rolls. I chat with locals as I devour a chicken and egg roll, wrapping up my street food journey in true Kolkata style.

title: Pure Bihari Non Vegetarian Food I Dabbu Egg Poach + Champaran Style Mutton + Kadha Masala Chicken
description:
In this episode of Delhi Community Food Stories, we find ourselves in a warm, inviting home kitchen, immersed in the flavours and memories of a quintessential Bihari non-vegetarian feast. The host, a passionate professional and fellow food lover, brings together family recipes and everyday rituals in a meal that speaks of tradition, comfort, and community.

The experience began with a refreshing glass of saunf ka sharbat — subtly sweet, fragrant, and deeply nostalgic. As conversations flowed, we moved to the first dish of the day: dabbu poach, a beloved street food from Patna. Made in a ladle-like vessel known as a dabbu, this zesty egg snack was fun to prepare and even more fun to devour — a reminder of Bihar’s vibrant roadside food culture.

As the kitchen filled with aromas, preparations began for the main course. Mutton was set aside to marinate for a slow-cooked Champaran-style dish — bold, smoky, and spiced with intention. Meanwhile, a khada masala chicken came to life on the stove — a semi-dry dish infused with the deep fragrance of whole spices, offering warmth in every bite.

The meal continued with rohu fish marinated in a mustard, garlic, and red chilli paste. Cooked in a tomato-based gravy enriched with the classic mustard blend and tempered with panch phoran, the fish curry brought a beautiful balance of heat and tang. There were also crispy fish roe pakoras — a seasonal delicacy that added texture and surprise to the platter.

What unfolded over the next few hours was more than a cooking session. It was a window into the culinary culture of Bihar, where food is layered with stories, memories, and care. Each dish carried a distinct voice — some bold, some quiet — but all rooted in the idea of home.

This episode is a celebration of shared meals, everyday expertise, and the quiet pride that lives in home kitchens. Through spice-laden pots and heartfelt conversations, it offers a glimpse into how food continues to connect, comfort, and carry culture forward — one lovingly prepared plate at a time.

About Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah:

The show is inspired from the famous humorous column 'Duniya Ne Undha Chasma' written by the eminent Gujarati writer Mr. Tarak Mehta. This story revolves around daily happenings in "Gokuldham Co-operative Society" and covers topical issues which are socially relevant. The show predominantly - revolves around 'Jethalal' who is an uneducated Gujarati businessman. Your 'Taarak Mehta', is his neighbor. 'Jethalal' finds a friend and philosopher in 'Taarak Mehta' and often goes to him for advice whenever he is in trouble. Jethalaal's family includes his simpleton wife 'Daya Ben' and a mischievous son 'Tapu'. Tapu is a menace and a constant source of trouble to all the members of Gokuldham. They have often warned 'Jethalal' to reform 'Tapu' or else be prepared to leave the premises. Lost hopes of being heard by his son push Jethalal' to call his father 'Champaklal' from the village. This was his great idea of leashing some control over the mischievous Tapu. The opposite happens and the grandfather joins hands with the grandson to make life a roller coaster troublesome ride for Jethalal.

title: India's Best Butter Chicken is on the Streets of Delhi | Street Eats | Bon Appétit
description:
Bon Appétit joins Chef Meherwan Irani to explore Delhi’s street food scene at Aslam Chicken. Located in Old Delhi, Aslam Chicken is serving butter chicken–but it’s not the butter chicken you would expect. Grilled over charcoal on a rooftop, marinated with yoghurt and spices, this dish is finished off with a drenching of cream and astonishing amounts of butter. Considered the predecessor of the butter chicken we know so well, Old Delhi-style butter chicken perfectly showcases the skill, technique, and drama of Delhi street food.

About Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah: 
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The show is inspired by the famous humorous column 'Duniya Ne Undha Chasma' by the eminent Gujarati writer Mr. Tarak Mehta. This story evolves around happenings in "Gokuldham Co-operative Society" and covers topical issues that are socially relevant. The show predominantly - revolves around 'Jethalal' (Dilip Joshi), an uneducated Gujarati businessman. Your 'Taarak Mehta' (Sailesh Lodha), is his neighbour. 'Jethalal' finds a friend and philosopher in 'Taarak Mehta' and often goes to him for advice whenever he is in trouble. Jethalal's family includes his simpleton wife 'Daya Ben' (Disha Wakani) and a mischievous son 'Tapu' (Bhavya Gandhi). Tapu is a menace and a constant source of trouble for all the members of Gokuldham. They have often warned 'Jethalal' to reform 'Tapu' or be prepared to leave the premises. Lost hopes of being heard by his son, he calls his father 'Champaklal' (Amit Bhatt) from the village. This was his great idea of leashing some control over the mischievous Tapu. The opposite happens and the grandfather joins hands with the grandson to make life a roller coaster troublesome ride for Jethalal.

title: Full Day Of Delhi’s Best Food In ₹1000?! 🤯🔥
description:
A full day of eating in Delhi on just ₹1000 — and somehow this city still delivered big flavour without breaking the budget. From a classic old-Delhi style breakfast to some iconic spots across the capital, this one was a proper DCT-style food run.

The morning began with crispy, hot bedmi pooris paired with hearty sabzi — the kind of breakfast that immediately sets the tone for the day. Lunch took me to Khan Market, where a punchy masala shikanji and a melt-in-your-mouth mutton seekh roll reminded me why Delhi owns the North Indian grill game. As the city turned golden in the evening, I stopped by Humayunpur for some juicy momos that absolutely slapped.

And to wrap up the challenge, I ended the night at the OG Rajinder Dhaba with their iconic butter chicken and garlic naan — the happiest way to close a ₹1000 food day. Delhi never disappoints.

The protagonists of the serial are an elite group of police officers belonging to the Crime Investigation Department of the police force, led by ACP Pradyuman [ played by the dynamic Shivaji Satam ]. title: The ORIGINAL Hyderabadi Dum Biryani | Bawarchi Restaurant | Globally Famous Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
description:
The ORIGINAL Hyderabadi Dum Biryani | Bawarchi Restaurant | Globally Famous Hyderabadi Dum Biryani

Today is the beginning of our Hyderabad Food Series. We wanted to start the series with a BANG. Hyderabad is know for its Dum Biryani which is World Famous. Bawarchi Restaurant is World famous when it comes to quality and quantity with the most reasonable pricing. I met the owner's and found out that their motive is to let everyone enjoy the authentic hyderabadi biryani without thinking much about their pocket/budget. Hyderabad street food is know for its culture spices and basmati rice. The place is overly packed through out the year and Ramazan is like a MELA. Bawarchi Restaurant begun 30 Years ago and they only have one branch where we visited. They serve a lot in the menu and we ordered for their Iconic Hyderabadi Chicken Dum Biryani, Hyderabadi Mutton Dum Biryani, Chicken 65, Prawns 65. The service was quick. They have been awarded by many major platforms, media Etc. I was accompanied by Murtuza from BeingHydFoodie who has great knowledge of food. Hyderabad food series has just begun and Bawarchi Restaurant made its start.

title: 🇰🇷 Korean Street Food HEAVEN in Seoul Myeongdong & Gwangjang Market
description:
⭐⭐⭐ English subtitles are always available, just click the "CC" on the screen 😊

Hello, I'm Alin.
This installment of our food tour comes to Seoul, South Korea!

Myeongdong Night Market in Seoul, where the neon lights are flashing and the aroma is overflowing!
Flame steak, beef on the iron plate, drizzled with sauce and then flames rise, a double blow to the eyes and tastebuds! Classic Korean fried chicken, crispy skin covered in sweet and spicy sauce! Fish cake skewers and fried rice cakes with spicy sauce are a must-try when you're in Korea. Soft rice cakes with sweet and spicy sauce instantly activate the taste buds! The cheesy kimchi gochujang has the right blend of local and western cheeses!

Seoul's Gwangjang Market, the mecca of traditional Korean cuisine!
Raw marinated crabs with sweet crab meat as smooth as jelly! With traditional food stalls all over the market, experience the delicious flavors while getting into the atmosphere of native Korean food!

DELHI VLOG: Dilli Ka Street Food & Markets | Connaught Place to Jama Masjid | RAMSHA SULTAN
description:
Welcome to Dilwalo Ki Dilli, the heart of India 🇮🇳. In this video, I take you through some of the most iconic, aesthetic, and soulful spots of New Delhi and Old Delhi — from the colonial charm of Cannaught Place to the narrow food-filled lanes of Jama Masjid, the high-end vibes of Khan Market, to the desi bazaar energy of Lajpat Nagar Market. I even visited  Jamia Millia Islamia University as a Guest Speaker.
So, get ready for a full Dilli darshan!

8:40 Delhi Street Food

📍1. Connaught Place (CP) – Delhi’s Colonial Heartbeat
Explore the colonial charm of Connaught Place Delhi aka CP — a hub for shopping in Palika Bazar, relaxing in Central Park, and experiencing the top things to do in Connaught Place. A perfect mix of heritage and modern vibes.

🛍️2. Janpath Market – Trendy Shopping on a Budget
Head to Janpath Market Delhi for the ultimate budget shopping in Delhi! Find Kolhapuri chappals, silver jewellery, boho bags, and everything trendy at this iconic Janpath street market.

☕3. Depauls – Delhi’s OG Cold Coffee Spot Since 1952
Tucked inside Janpath Bhawan, Deepauls Janpath serves the best cold coffee in Delhi. A must-try hidden gem among Janpath food spots and classic hidden gems CP.

🛒4. Khan Market – Where Delhi’s Elite Hang Out
Discover Khan Market Delhi — perfect for luxury shopping in Delhi, sipping at the best cafés in Khan Market, and browsing through the best bookstores in Delhi. It’s where elegance meets heritage.

🇮🇳5. India Gate – A Tribute to India’s Bravery.
Witness the iconic India Gate night view and pay tribute at Amar Jawan Jyoti. A must-see Delhi landmark and one of the top must visit places in Delhi for tourists.

🧕6. Jama Masjid & Purani Dilli – Spiritual + Culinary Heaven
Feel the power of faith at Jama Masjid Delhi, followed by a mouth-watering Old Delhi food crawl. Watch me explore Jama Masjid street food and the best Muslim Halal food in Delhi.

🎓7. Jamia Millia Islamia University – A Campus Full of Culture
Jamia Millia Islamia University is one of the top Muslim universities in India, known for its rich history, academic excellence, and vibrant campus life. 
I was honored to be invited as a guest speaker at the Engineering Department’s Entrepreneurship Event, where I shared my content creator and business journey. The warm meet and greet with students and glimpses of Jamia campus life made this visit truly special.

🧣8. Lajpat Nagar Market – The Desi Fashion Hub
From Indian suits to readymade anarkalis, Lajpat Nagar shopping is a dream! Tried the famous Ram Laddoo in Lajpat Nagar.

This vlog is not just about tourism, it’s about reliving memories, discovering hidden gems, and falling in love with Delhi all over again.

title: Delhi's Dilli Haat HIDDEN Food Secrets You Never Knew | Veggie Paaji
description:
Join Veggie Paaji on an epic multi state food tour at Dilli Haat, INA, Delhi! In this video, we embark on a culinary journey to explore the diverse and authentic vegetarian cuisines from Jammu & Kashmir, Odisha, Maharashtra, and Sikkim, all under one roof.

Highlights of our food adventure:

Wazwan (Jammu & Kashmir Food Stall): Savor the rich flavors of Jammu Rajma Rice Thali [02:34], including authentic Baddarwah Rajma, flavorful Dam Aloo, and fried Paneer.

Nimantran (Odisha Food Stall): Experience the traditional Odia delicacy, Dahi Pakhala (fermented rice with curd) [06:58], served with various side dishes.

Maharashtra Food Stall (MTDC): Indulge in the rustic taste of Pithla Bhakri Thali [12:07] and refresh with a unique Kokam Sharbat [12:15]. Don't miss the creamy Shrikhand [12:14]!

Sikkim Tourism Tashi Delek Food Stall: Delight in perfectly steamed Veg Momos [17:23] served with a comforting clear soup.

This video is a celebration of India's incredible food diversity, providing an honest review and helping you navigate the best of Dilli Haat, INA.

title: TOP 10 BEST PLACES IN GHAZIABAD | Delhi NCR के पास घूमने की बेस्ट जगहें | 10ON10
description:
Ghaziabad, located near Delhi and Noida, is a fast-growing city known for its mix of culture, shopping, and leisure. It's a part of the NCR (National Capital Region), making it easy to visit from New Delhi or India Gate. There are many famous places in Ghaziabad that attract locals and tourists alike. Whether you're making a daily vlog or a family vlog, you’ll find great spots to explore. title: Manali Apple Orchard Farm Food Tour I Manu Temple + Hidimba Temple + Nepali Thakali Food and Momo
description:
Our last day in Manali unfolded like a slow, comforting melody full of simple pleasures, heartfelt encounters, and flavours that capture the soul of the mountains.

We began the morning at Hotellier, tucking into a basic yet genuinely satisfying breakfast. Nothing extravagant, just honest, comforting food that lifted the spirits as the cold mountain air wrapped around us.

From there, the path led us to the peaceful surroundings of the Hidimba Temple, where towering deodar trees and soft sunlight filtered through like a blessing. The calmness of the shrine set the tone for the day as we walked through its sacred precincts.

A short drive away, the vibes shifted entirely as we entered the bohemian lanes of Old Manali, the cafes, the bustle, the little shops, and the unmistakable charm that travellers always return for. And right in the middle of that cheerful chaos, we met someone unforgettable: a 100-year-old lady selling khumani. Sitting quietly beside her modest display of apricots, she welcomed us with the warmest smile. 

Our next pause was at the German Bakery and Nepali Sandwich Bar, where we picked up a few cookies, sweet, simple bites that kept us going. This was followed by a hearty mealtime stop at Darjeeling Steamers. Their Nepali offerings were truly the highlight: a comforting Nepali thali, flavourful jhol momos, and sesame oil momos that carried the warmth of home-cooked food.

The journey then took us to Mosum Retreat, a hidden haven surrounded by orchards heavy with plums and apples. The sight of trees laden with fruit felt like stepping into nature’s own pantry. Here, we were welcomed by Tarna Devi, who invited us into her world with open arms. In the orchard-side kitchen, she guided us through the making of traditional snacks, childu and giche, each prepared with a simplicity and authenticity that only the hands of experience can offer.

As the day softened into evening light, we accompanied her on a short walk to her village home nearby. The warmth of her hospitality, the stories she shared, and the serene mountain backdrop made it a moment of deep connection, an experience that beautifully tied together our time in Manali.
